A United States jury has found Chinese tech giant Huawei and three of its subsidiaries gui
items.text:
US court convicts Huawei of theft: A history of Chinese firm’s global woes
Chinese tech giant has also faced legal problems from Europe to Asia while its products have been banned during trade war with the US.
A United States jury has found Chinese tech giant Huawei and three of its subsidiaries guilty of serious violations, including defrauding banks and conspiracy to steal trade secrets from US firms.
The verdict on Tuesday was handed down in a New York federal court and came after a lengthy trial of the Chinese electronics and tech giant.
Huawei faced multiple allegations, including accusations of engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy. But the company’s troubles extend as well to a number of other countries, including Canada and Australia.
“For over two decades, Huawei built its global empire on a foundation of fraud, theft and deception,” said Assistant Attorney General A Tysen Duva of the Criminal Division of the US Department of Justice.
“Huawei’s crimes threatened the US financial system, took advantage of American companies that compete honestly in the global telecommunications market and undermined our national security.”
Here’s what we know:
What was Huawei convicted of?
Huawei was convicted on 10 of 11 counts along with its Chinese subsidiary Huawei Device Co Ltd and US subsidiaries Futurewei Technologies Inc and Huawei Device USA Inc.
The jury found them guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, conspiracy to commit wire and bank fraud, wire fraud, bank fraud, conspiracy to defraud the United States, conspiracy to violate the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), substantive violations of IEEPA and money laundering conspiracy.
In a statement, the US Justice Department revealed specific instances of alleged misconduct.
A Huawei employee stole information about Tappy, a robot developed by T-Mobile, although both firms had signed a nondisclosure agreement, the department alleged.
In another instance, Huawei engineers were accused of copying the source code of Cisco routers.
Another employee allegedly disguised as someone else went to work for the US tech company CNEX even though the firm had earlier indicated it did not want to work directly with Huawei.
The convictions also related to allegations that Huawei operated in Iran and North Korea, countries under US sanctions, and made false statements to US officials and banks to hide that fact.
Huawei, however, was acquitted of the most serious charge: engaging in criminal racketeering conspiracy.
Criminal charges were first brought against the company in 2019. Its lawyers said investigators used isolated cases of wrongdoing by a few employees to paint a grand conspiracy.
Sentencing is set for September although Huawei’s lawyers said the company will appeal.
Huawei is expected to pay huge sums in penalties.
Is this part of the US-China tech tussle?
Yes. Washington and Beijing are in a race to command technological advancements, particularly artificial intelligence.
Beijing has condemned the verdict as an attempt by Washington aimed at “containing and suppressing” Chinese firms.
“The Chinese government firmly opposes movies by the US side aimed at containing and suppressing Chinese enterprises, and firmly supports Chinese enterprises’ lawful rights,” the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement on Wednesday.
The verdict was announced as the Nvidia scandal has been rocking Silicon Valley. Jensen Huang, the cofounder and CEO of the advanced chips company, is under US investigation for potentially leaking critical information to China after it was revealed a woman he had a romantic relationship with could have been a Chinese spy.
Beijing has denied involvement.
Nvidia’s chips power AI products, and Washington has restricted the company from selling its most advanced semiconductors to China. Nvidia is the world’s second most valuable company after only Apple with a market capitalisation of more than $4.4 trillion.
What issues does Huawei face elsewhere?
For years, the company has been blacklisted in the US, where it is restricted from selling equipment to telecommunications carriers without special approval because of security concerns.
Other US allies have flagged it over concerns that the company is too close to Chinese authorities:
- Australia and New Zealand – joined the US in banning the firm from supplying 5G equipment and services in 2018.
- Britain – banned telecom providers from buying new Huawei 5G equipment after 2020 and set a deadline of 2027 to remove all existing Huawei gear from networks.
- Canada – barred Huawei from supplying equipment for 4G and 5G networks in 2022. In 2018, Canadian authorities arrested Meng Wanzhou, the chief financial officer and daughter of founder Ren Zhengfei. She was extradited to the US, where she faced allegations of misleading an HSBC banker about Huawei’s business in Iran. Charges were later dropped, and Meng returned to China in a prisoner swap.
- Europe – In 2024, major German providers like Deutsche Telekom agreed to remove Chinese-made telecom equipment from 5G networks, including those from Huawei and ZTE, another Chinese manufacturer, before a 2029 deadline. Germany is also preparing sweeping bans on Chinese mobile network equipment that essentially could bar Huawei and ZTE. Other countries – including Estonia, Denmark, France, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Portugal, Romania and Sweden – have outright banned or restricted Huawei and other Chinese manufacturers.
- Japan, Taiwan and India – have also either completely excluded or restricted the company.

items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 25 – Twenty-four people charged alongside controversial preacher Paul Mackenzie have been acquitted of all charges, while 12 others have been convicted of various offences against children.
In a judgment delivered on Wednesday, Principal Magistrate N. Chepchirchir found Mackenzie
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 25 – Twenty-four people charged alongside controversial preacher Paul Mackenzie have been acquitted of all charges, while 12 others have been convicted of various offences against children.
In a judgment delivered on Wednesday, Principal Magistrate N. Chepchirchir found Mackenzie and 11 co-accused guilty of offences ranging from assault occasioning actual bodily harm to cruelty to children and infringement of children’s right to education.
Mackenzie was convicted of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and five counts of cruelty to a child.
Other accused persons were found guilty of various counts of cruelty to children, while some were convicted of violating children’s right to education.
Those acquitted include the sixth, eighth, ninth, tenth, 12th to 24th, 26th, 28th to 31st, 35th and 36th accused persons.
The court ordered that those acquitted be released unless they are being held over other matters.
All the accused persons were also acquitted of the torture charges, with the court finding them guilty only on the specific counts outlined in its judgment.
The convicted accused persons will appear in court on December 15 for mitigation before sentencing.
The Probation and Aftercare Service will prepare pre-sentence reports to guide the court in determining appropriate sentences.

items.title: Mulder shreds Bangladesh as South Africa seal 2-0 sweep before England Tests
items.summary:
South Africa thrash Bangladesh to seal 2-0 sweep before England Test series as Wiaan Mulder takes seven-wicket haul
South Africa host England in a three-Test series live on Sky Sports from December 17, with matches at Johannesburg, Centurion and Cape Town; Proteas hammer Bangladesh inside three days
items.text:
South Africa thrash Bangladesh to seal 2-0 sweep before England Test series as Wiaan Mulder takes seven-wicket haul
South Africa host England in a three-Test series live on Sky Sports from December 17, with matches at Johannesburg, Centurion and Cape Town; Proteas hammer Bangladesh inside three days at SuperSport Park to consolidate top spot in World Test Championship
Wednesday 25 November 2026 13:54, UK
South Africa's Wiaan Mulder followed his fifth Test century with career-best bowling figures of 7-31 as the Proteas routed Bangladesh by an innings and 219 runs inside three days to secure a 2-0 sweep ahead of their three-match series versus England.
Mulder's knock of 100 from 178 balls came in the hosts' 494-7 declared at Centurion, before the tourists were rolled for 184 in their second dig, having been blown away for 91 on day one of the game when Kagiso Rabada and Marco Jansen shared six wickets.
South Africa, who face England at home in Tests for the first time since 2020 when the opening game takes place in Johannesburg from December 17, consolidated their position at the top of the World Test Championship as they target back-to-back titles.
- Scorecard: South Africa vs Bangladesh, second Test match
- Listen to latest episode of the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast
- Latest Sky Sports deals or stream contract-free with NOW
The Proteas beat Australia in the Lord's final in 2025, the same side they recently defeated 2-1 in a three-match assignment on home turf after rallying from 1-0 down.
South Africa then saw off Bangladesh by nine wickets in the opening Test at Wanderers, a game in which Mulder was out for a two-ball duck in his sole hit, before this drubbing at SuperSport Park ended when Mulder caught Tigers tailender Khaled Ahmed off Jansen.
Bangladesh battled to 58-0 in their second innings, only to lose two wickets for no runs and three for 20 once Tanzid Hasan (29) edged Mulder behind on the cut, with Mominul Haque (0) glancing the same bowler down the leg-side two overs later.
Once Rabada reduced the visitors to 158-5 by having top-scorer Towhid Hridoy (41) clip meekly to gully, Mulder shredded the middle and lower order.
The all-rounder bowled four other players, including Jaker Ali (2) and Shoriful Islam (0) from successive deliveries, and forced captain Najmul Hossain Shanto (34) to nick off as he found lavish swing movement while bagging a maiden Test five-for.
Mulder said: "I got the ball to go with the wind, into the right hander, away from the left hander, and I kind of just stuck with that. I tried to target top it off stump as often as I could.
"With a little bit of extra movement, I think I got them playing at balls that they shouldn't, and they created a gap in there to hit the stumps."
Shanto added: "We knew that conditions are tough. Our batters couldn't adapt, especially in the first innings."

items.title: NACADA Secures Historic Conviction in Major Drug Trafficking Case
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 25 — The National Authority for the Campaign Against Alcohol and Drug Abuse (NACADA) has secured a historic conviction in the fight against narcotics trafficking.
In a ruling delivered Wednesday before Hon. Stephen Ngii (SPMS) at the JKIA Law Courts, Samson Gathuki Njeri was conv
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 25 — The National Authority for the Campaign Against Alcohol and Drug Abuse (NACADA) has secured a historic conviction in the fight against narcotics trafficking.
In a ruling delivered Wednesday before Hon. Stephen Ngii (SPMS) at the JKIA Law Courts, Samson Gathuki Njeri was convicted for trafficking in narcotic drugs, marking a significant victory for the Authority’s ongoing crackdown on illicit substances.
Njeri was ordered to pay a fine of Ksh. 50 million or, in default, serve 20 years imprisonment.
The conviction follows an arrest made on December 20, 2025, at Kimbo backstreet area in Juja, within Kiambu County, by NACADA enforcement officers and officers from the National Anti-Narcotics Investigation Bureau (NANIB) attached to NACADA.During the arrest, officers recovered 96 packages containing dry plant material suspected to be narcotics, alongside Sh6,600 believed to be proceeds of crime.
Forensic analysis established the gross weight of the recovered substance at 4,510.08 grams, with an estimated market value of Sh135,302.40.
Following the ruling, the court ordered theSh 6,600 to be forfeited to the State. The narcotic exhibits are to be destroyed after the expiry of 14 days, except samples retained for record purposes.
Speaking after the ruling, NACADA CEO Dr. Anthony Omerikwa thanked the judiciary for its support. “We thank the judiciary for complementing the Authority’s efforts in the fight against drug abuse in the country. This conviction is a strong message to those involved in the drug trade that they will face the full wrath of the law,” Dr. Omerikwa said.
The CEO also commended the community for its role in the case. “I commend the community for volunteering information that led to this momentous arrest and conviction. Community vigilance is critical in the fight against drug abuse, and this outcome demonstrates what can be achieved when citizens work with enforcement agencies.”
Omerikwa reiterated NACADA’s commitment to ensuring that those who profit from the drug trade are brought to justice.

NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 25 – A habeas corpus application has been filed at the Milimani Law Courts seeking the production and release of Abdiaziz Molu, popularly known as Zizzou, who is reportedly missing following an alleged abduction six months ago.
Embakasi East MP Babu Owino announced that he was representing Molu in the court proceedings, seeking orders compelling authorities to account for his whereabouts.
Owino accused the government of failing to address alleged abductions and demanded an end to the practice.
The MP said the application was intended to secure Molu’s immediate production before the court and release.
“We are sending a strong message to the Government: these abductions must stop. If the Government fails to end this practice and account for those abducted, we will mobilise our people for peaceful protests in Nairobi CBD,” the Embakasi East MP stated.

Max Calce made the surprise announcement that he would be moving to the Brantford Bulldogs of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL) in a statement issued on the website of his German Ice Hockey League (DEL) team, Adler Mannh
items.text:
German ice hockey prospect Max Calce leaves Mannheim for Canada
November 25, 2026
Max Calce made the surprise announcement that he would be moving to the Brantford Bulldogs of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL) in a statement issued on the website of his German Ice Hockey League (DEL) team, Adler Mannheim late on Tuesday.
"I have long had three goals," he said. "To play for the Adler, in the Canadian Hockey League (CHL), and in the NHL. Today is a difficult and emotional day for me, as I say goodbye to my home."
Having started the season in Mannheim, many thought the 17-year-old would finish the season in the DEL.
The announcement came after Calce, who had been a regular in Mannheim's lineup this season, had been left off the team sheet for Tuesday night's game in Straubing.
This comes less than a month after he became the youngest-ever player to score a goal for the German men's national team – against Slovakia in Germany's final game of the annual Deutschland Cup invitational.
Mature decision-making on the ice
"It was only a matter of time; he's an incredible player," said former NHL player Tobias Rieder, who frequently played on a line with Calce during the tournament.
"The most impressive thing is that, at 17, he plays a very mature style of hockey—he almost always makes the right decision."
Calce is also the youngest goal scorer in DEL history, having found the net for Mannheim in September 2025 at just 16 years and 100 days old.
In his statement, the centerman thanked Mannheim, which has produced a number of NHL players over the years, including Leon Draisaitl, Moritz Seider and Tim Stützle.
"The trust, support, and experiences I gained through my coaches, teammates, and everyone within the organization have played a major role in my development—both as a player and as a person."
This season, his second in the DEL, Calce has six goals and two assists in Mannheim's first 19 games.
"We believe in preparing young players to take opportunities at the highest level of the sport," Dallas Eakins, Mannheim's head coach and sporting director said.
"As much as we would have loved to continue to have him play for us, we respect and welcome his ambition."
Increased visibility ahead of NHL draft
On the surface, the notion of moving from a men's professional league to a junior league may seem like a step backwards, but Calce's move to the OHL will give Calce increased exposure to NHL scouts. The OHL is one of the top three junior leagues in Canada and according to figures released by the CHL last season, they produce more NHL players than any other developmental system.
In doing so, Calce is now following the path of Edmonton Oilers superstar Draisaitl, who left Mannheim's youth program at the age of 16 to pursue his NHL dream, joining the Western Hockey League's Prince Albert Raiders.
This, of course is not the only path to the NHL; Moritz Seider of the Detroit Red Wings and the Ottawa Senators' Tim Stützle were both first-round draft choices plucked directly from Mannheim. Calce is hoping to be taken in the first round of next summer's NHL Entry Draft.
Born to Russian parents in Mannheim, Calce changed his birth surname, Penkin, to that of his mother and stepfather last summer.

The 31-year-old, from Berkshire, who later
items.text:
Sterling given suspended sentence for dangerous driving
- Published
Former England footballer Raheem Sterling has been given a suspended sentence after admitting dangerously driving his Lamborghini while inhaling nitrous oxide from a balloon on a motorway.
The 31-year-old, from Berkshire, who later crashed into a metal gate during rush hour, gave no reaction as he was handed a 12-month jail term, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court.
Sterling had pleaded guilty to dangerous driving of a Lamborghini Urus and possessing nitrous oxide on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road on 28 May
The judge said Sterling's use of the Class C drug had became a "maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period" in his career.
Sterling, who left the court without making any comment, was ordered to complete 100 hours unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months.
He was arrested after crashing near the M3 in Hampshire.
- Raheem Sterling - from national icon to suspended jail sentence 
  - Published50 minutes ago
District judge Kirsty Allman told the court on Wednesday that Sterling made a "deliberate and entirely selfish decision" to drive his vehicle "without adequate sleep" and whilst consuming nitrous oxide, commonly known as laughing gas.
She said this exposed a "large number of road users to a significant risk of serious harm by the manner of your driving on two motorways and in peak travel time that morning".
During the September hearing, prosecutor Simon Jones said a number of calls were made between 07:45 and 08:52 BST about a black sports car and the manner it was being driven.
Witness Christopher Jennings called 999 after driving alongside Sterling's car on the M25, and "he was shocked by what he saw", Jones said, and made clear "he sighted the defendant inhaling from the balloon".
Fiona Jennings – driving on the southbound M3 – described the driving as "absolutely horrendous" and "swerving in and out of lanes", the court heard.
The court heard Sterling strayed into the central reservation of the M3, exited at junction 4A, and veered off the A327, crashing into a metal gate near a layby.
His vehicle sustained "substantial damage to the tyres and bodywork and was no longer capable of being driven", the court heard.
Sterling was taken to Basingstoke police investigation centre by officers, where he disclosed he had a "problem with nitrous oxide", said Jones.
He complied with an impairment test, but for a blood sample, Sterling asked to obtain legal advice before making a decision.
In the police sergeant's view "he was deliberately failing to provide a clear answer".
Sterling was later interviewed by police with legal representation present where he accepted he had been the driver and provided no comment answers about the driving.
Defending Sterling on Wednesday, Jason Bartfeld KC said there was no dispute that this was a "top category case" because of prolonged driving and "at times" serious impairment which would have been short periods within the driving.
But the defence did not accept the damage to the car was serious and said there was "confusion" over the failure to provide a specimen.
District Judge Kirsty Allman said: "I accept that your character has been positively exemplary.
"You enjoyed a highly successful professional football career and were widely regarded as a role model for many young people through your achievements and public profile."
He was given credit for his guilty pleas.
Sterling most recently played for Feyenoord in the Dutch Eredivisie, having left Chelsea in January, but made just eight appearances in the Netherlands.
In four years at Chelsea - including a season-long loan at Arsenal - he made 59 league appearances after signing from Manchester City in 2022.
With City he won four Premier League titles, having started his senior career with Liverpool before moving to Manchester in 2015.
He is currently without a club.
In the 2021 Queen's Birthday Honours, Sterling was made an MBE for services to racial equality in sport.

items.text:
Why Indians are still ending up in Russia's war
November 25, 2026
Gurpreet Singh Randhawa, a 40-year-old from Jalandhar in India's northern Punjab state, said he traveled to Russia for work after responding to a Facebook advertisement for a driving job at a garment factory.
But instead of finding work as a driver, he was sent to fight in Ukraine for the Russian armed forces.
After escaping from his unit, he surrendered to Ukrainian forces in November. He is now being held as a prisoner of war.
In an interview with Ukrainian YouTuber Volodymyr Zolkin, Randhawa described how, after arriving in Russia, he was taken to a military facility, made to sign a contract and sent for training. He said they confiscated his passport and phone. His account has not been independently verified.
Randhawa's story is a familiar one in India.
He is the second Indian national known to have escaped the Russian military. Sahil Majothi, a 23-year-old from Gujarat, surrendered to Ukrainian forces in October 2025. He had joined the Russian military while serving a prison sentence in Russia, reportedly believing that military service would help him secure his release.
India's efforts to bring recruits home
The cases underline how little has changed since Prime Minister Narendra Modi raised the issue with Russian President Vladimir Putin during his visit to Moscow in July 2024.
At the time, Putin assured him that Indians who were misled into joining the Russian army would be discharged. But the recruitment of Indians has continued.
In an October filing before the Supreme Court, India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said approximately 267 Indians have joined the Russian armed forces since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Of these, 139 were discharged and 51 were killed. The whereabouts of the 77 others were unknown. Russian authorities have confirmed that seven of them are missing.
The problem extends beyond Indians who travel to Russia seeking civilian employment, only to find themselves exposed to recruitment networks and the dangers of a war zone.
The MEA has also highlighted cases of Indians knowingly enlisting in the Russian military for the supposed financial benefits on offer, believing they could later secure release through government intervention.
Some had also approached Indian authorities to renounce their citizenship and obtain Russian passports. "This is a dangerous path and is strongly discouraged by the government," the ministry said.
Duped or desperate?
Former diplomat Anil Trigunayat said the growing movement of Indian workers to Russia presents both economic opportunities and new challenges for their protection.
"Inadequate oversight of recruitment networks could leave vulnerable workers exposed to exploitation," Trigunayat told DW.
He said Indian workers were often burdened by substantial recruitment fees and continued deductions from their salaries by intermediaries.
"Some of them had paid between 300,000 to 500,000 Indian rupees [$5,400 /€4,900] to Indian recruitment agents, and even while working in Russia, more than 30% of their agreed monthly salary was taken away by local and foreign agents," Trigunayat said.
The former diplomat added that some Indians who had overstayed their visas in Russia were particularly vulnerable. Military service was allegedly offered to earn substantial wages and regularize their immigration status.
Mohammad Sufiyan, from Hyderabad in the southern state of Telangana, said he was lured to Russia under false pretences and forced into active combat in Ukraine.
He had traveled abroad in search of employment and a better livelihood, but ended up in a war zone. He has since returned home to India.
"Many people are duped. Some decide it is better to seek citizenship than come back to India. It's a tough life, and people will go to any lengths to get some sort of employment," Sufiyan told DW.
Sufiyan's experience points to the economic desperation that makes such offers attractive, even when they carry the risk of being caught up in a war.
Rajan Kumar, a professor at the Centre for Russian and Central Asian Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University's School of International Studies, said some Indians who traveled to Russia for work could find themselves caught up in the fighting without having joined the military.
"Some of them, they don't join the army, but they end up in the army region. They're caught in the crossfire," Kumar told DW.
He said India was negotiating with Moscow to secure the return of its citizens caught up in such situations. "Russia is very cooperative so far," he said.
Moscow prioritizes military aims over strategic diplomacy
India has been pressing Russia to take action, but the issue persists.
The recruitment efforts reflect Russia's need for more manpower for its nearly five-year war in Ukraine , and the limited influence New Delhi can exert over Moscow, despite the close political relationship between the two countries.
Mohsin Raza Khan, a professor at the Jindal School of International Affairs, told DW that Putin's need to sustain the war effort was taking precedence over the concerns of a strategic partner.
He points out that the Russian president was reluctant to impose another mobilization on his own population for fear of domestic unrest.
"In these circumstances, sustaining the war effort appears to take precedence over concerns raised by India. Neither Modi nor New Delhi has sufficient leverage to change that," said Khan.
Khan also said the willingness of some Indians to enlist, and even consider giving up their citizenship, is down to the lack of decent employment opportunities at home.
"For young, educated men without contacts or connections, the chances of respectable employment are so low that the risks of a high casualty war are preferable," he said.

items.text:
‘Second home’: Why Israel is celebrating Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia
Israel’s tech sector and economy have strong ties to chip giant Nvidia, which invests billions of dollars.
When Jensen Huang returned to lead the chip giant Nvidia this week after a scandal over his extramarital affairs, US President Donald Trump was not the only head of government to welcome his second coming.
Thousands of kilometres away, Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was celebrating too.
Huang once called Israel Nvidia’s “second home”, and Netanyahu reflected that feeling as he wrote on X: “Nvidia’s partnership with Israel’s tech sector has created enormous value for the company and for Israel’s innovation economy.”
“Continuity in Nvidia’s leadership is good news for that partnership and for the global AI industry,” Netanyahu added, referring to Huang’s reinstatement as CEO and president on Monday.
Global headlines have focused on Huang’s affairs, including with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset; his resignation’s implications for the AI industry; and the larger technology race between Washington and Beijing. His reinstatement at the company he cofounded has gone a long way to settle market jitters. Nvidia’s share price rocketed up by 30 percent on Monday.
But Huang’s return has also calmed nerves in Israel – arguably the country most impacted by Nvidia’s performance outside the United States as it hosts the US-based company’s largest overseas operations.
Here’s what we know:
Why is Nvidia important for Israel?
California-based Nvidia, the world’s most valuable semiconductor company with a market capitalisation of about $4 trillion, holds the key to the modern artificial intelligence revolution. Huang’s company holds an extraordinary near-90 percent share of the global market for GPUs – graphics processing units, which are specialised AI processors used in AI data centres.
Nvidia’s operations in Israel are its largest in research and development outside the US. It has doubled employees there in the past three years to 6,000 people across seven research and development centres in Yokne’am, Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, Ra’anana and Beersheba. It also has plans to build a major research and development campus in Kiryat Tivon near Haifa to accommodate up to 10,000 employees.
The Bank of Israel has estimated that Nvidia’s work in the country alone will add 2.2 percentage points of growth to Israel’s gross domestic product (GDP) in 2026, bringing it to 5.6 percent. Without Nvidia, that would be 3.4 percent growth, or 40 percent lower.
Next year, Nvidia is expected to add a further 2.4 percentage points to its GDP growth.
Nvidia paid about $1.29bn in taxes to Israel in its financial year that ended in January, according to its annual report. The company is projected to account for nearly 3 percent of Israel’s total state tax revenues in 2026, according to some estimates.
How did Israel react to Huang’s exit?
Huang’s resignation on November 12 initially rattled investors on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) with the benchmark indices sliding after the announcement.
But by the end of the day, they had recovered. The TA-35 index finished 0.22 per cent higher at the close of the day while the broader TA-125 gained 0.07 per cent. The BlueTech Global Index, which tracks technology companies, fell 0.15 per cent.
The Haaretz newspaper reported, however, that officials at Israel’s Ministry of Finance were concerned about the potential consequences for the Israeli economy of turmoil – and particularly Huang’s exit – at Nvidia.
On Monday, Israeli President Isaac Herzog congratulated Huang on his return, noting “his deep appreciation to Huang for his continued support for Israel and for his commitment to strengthening the connection between Nvidia and Israel”.
Herzog’s office said Huang told the president that he was “moved by the message and that he intends to make the most of the second chance he has been given”.
How important is Israel for Nvidia?
Nvidia is helping fuel Israel’s economic machine during its genocidal war on Gaza, pogroms by Israeli settlers against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and the occupation of southern Lebanon.
But Israel is also returning strong numbers for the company.
The root of the tech giant’s relationship with the country can be traced back to Nvidia’s acquisition of Mellanox, an Israeli company that supplies computer networking products, in April 2020 for nearly $7bn. That acquisition was central to Nvidia’s success.
Nvidia was already able to make powerful engines that process AI workloads, but a single GPU cannot handle that workload and needs to exchange information with other GPUs.
Mellanox made the networking infrastructure that allows those engines to work together at a fast pace, creating the foundational structure of a data centre.
Nvidia’s networking business, built around Mellanox, generated more than $21bn in revenues in the third quarter of 2026. That’s about 18 percent of Nvidia’s total quarterly revenue.
At the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas in January, Huang spoke about Israel’s role in the development of key Nvidia chips.
“Nvidia’s BlueField-4 DPU and three networking components – the ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, NVLink 6 Switch and Spectrum-6 Ethernet Switch – all came out of Israel. So four out of six chips came out of Israel,” he said, praising the employees in Israel.
“Pretty amazing and maybe next time, six out of six chips,” Huang added.
What is Nvidia’s role in Gaza?
A review by the American Friends Service Committee, a group that won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1947 partly for its work rescuing and providing relief to Jews during the Holocaust, has found that the Israeli military uses multiple Nvidia products.
Several purchases of Nvidia products were disclosed by the Israeli Ministry of Defence during Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, a report by the group last year noted.

items.title: Solomon Islands signs security deal with Australia
items.summary:
Solomon Islands signs security deal with Australia
Solomon Islands will have to consult Canberra before making new security or infrastructure deals under new pact.
Solomon Islands and Australia have signed a sweeping treaty affirming that the small Pacific country will allow no foreign military base
items.text:
Solomon Islands signs security deal with Australia
Solomon Islands will have to consult Canberra before making new security or infrastructure deals under new pact.
Solomon Islands and Australia have signed a sweeping treaty affirming that the small Pacific country will allow no foreign military bases on its territory.
The deal, signed on Wednesday, is seen as a blow to the regional ambitions of China, which had been moving closer to the Solomon Islands for years.
“Solomon Islands has been for a number of years a source of uncertainty and doubt in the region. Those days are gone,” Prime Minister Matthew Wale told journalists alongside his Australian counterpart Anthony Albanese.
The treaty establishes Australia as the island nation’s “primary security partner” and will see Canberra provide 740 million Australian dollars ($490m) over the next 10 years to fund free education and other programmes in Solomon Islands. Solomon Islands has a gross domestic product (GDP) of $1.75bn, according to the World Bank.
In exchange, Solomon Islands will allow no foreign military or security bases on its soil, and the country’s “sensitive” infrastructure will “remain free from militarisation, foreign interference and unauthorised access”.
That includes ports, airports, energy and telecommunications, as well as road and bridge construction – areas China has dominated in the islands through its Belt and Road Initiative. The deal will not apply retroactively.
Solomon Islands will also have to consult Australia before making deals involving its critical infrastructure or security cooperation unless it is with members of the Pacific Islands Forum regional bloc, Albanese said.
China relationship changing
Since being elected in May, Wale has upended Solomon Islands’ diplomatic moves towards China and realigned with Australia and the United States.
Asked about reports he had ended a secretive security pact with Beijing, Wale told journalists that discussions with China were “ongoing”.
China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs did not confirm whether the deal had been scrapped, but warned that the new agreement with Australia “should not target any third party”.
This is the latest in a string of similar deals Australia has struck with Pacific states, including Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu and Fiji.

items.title: Khawaja 'hurt' by 'personal attacks' from Cummins in sandpaper denials
items.summary:
Sandpapergate: Usman Khawaja 'hurt' by 'personal attacks' from Pat Cummins as he details Cameron Bancroft relationship
Usman Khawaja hopes there is collective responsibility for the Sandpapergate scandal in time and says current captain Pat Cummins still has the "opportunity of power"; former batter
items.text:
Sandpapergate: Usman Khawaja 'hurt' by 'personal attacks' from Pat Cummins as he details Cameron Bancroft relationship
Usman Khawaja hopes there is collective responsibility for the Sandpapergate scandal in time and says current captain Pat Cummins still has the "opportunity of power"; former batter says Cameron Bancroft feels like a "different person" after finally telling his side of ball-tampering saga
Wednesday 25 November 2026 13:00, UK
Usman Khawaja has told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast that he was "hurt" by Pat Cummins' "personal attacks" on him as the Australia Test captain explosively disputed his claims that every member of the side was aware of the use of sandpaper in 2018.
Khawaja made the allegations in his autobiography Sabr and they have since been backed up by David Warner and Cameron Bancroft - two of the players, along with then-skipper Steve Smith, who were slapped with bans following the ball-tampering plot in South Africa.
Cummins, part of the Australia bowling attack on that tour eight years ago, insisted he was not privy to the scheme when he and fellow quicks Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc, as well as spinner Nathan Lyon, released a joint-statement in 2021.
- Darren Lehmann denies knowledge of sandpaper use
- Cameron Bancroft article blows Sandpapergate open
- Listen to latest episode of Sky Sports Cricket Podcast
He then categorially denied knowledge earlier this month in a 68-minute press conference in which he accused Khawaja of being "casual" with people's lives.
Khawaja said in a chat with Michael Atherton and Nasser Hussain: "It was the most surprised I've been for a long time. I wasn't expecting that [from Cummins] whatsoever.
"I thought Pat had this really great opportunity to come out and bring everyone together. He's such a great leader. I've said in the book that I love the person he is, love the leader he is, so I thought if anyone can bring us together, it's Pat.
"I had hoped that he would - I text him before, trying do anything I could to make it easier, to do something to bring everyone in - but I realised that wasn't going to happen when he first started talking, so that was really sad.
"Then obviously the personal attacks were sad. I'm not going to lie about that, they hurt from a friend, someone you really respect. That wasn't very Pat Cummins-like, very different to the Pat Cummins I know, and it's hard for me to judge him on that.
"I know Pat, I know his family. They're beautiful, so it was really hard to reconcile the Pat I knew and the Pat that was attacking me personally rather than attacking what I'm saying. That was by far one of the toughest days I've ever experienced.
"I'll caveat that by saying that I have nothing but love for Pat. I don't judge people on certain instances or whatnot. That's not how I live my life. That's not how I function.
"Right now, are we talking? No, not really, but I've still got a lot of hope in my heart that at some stage if there's anyone that can bring everyone together, it's Pat. He's got the opportunity of power, whether it's now or later.
"But I think there was a perfect opportunity there if he took a softer route. He took a real harsh route and I think because of that everything just blew up after that like even more."
'It doesn't feel there is an ending right now and that sucks'
Khawaja wanted the team to take collective responsibility for the sandpaper plot at the time but says he was talked out of it by Smith as only the skipper, Warner and Bancroft - the player caught on camera looking to manipulate the ball - were suspended.
The 39-year-old, who retired from international cricket following Australia's 4-1 Ashes thrashing of England last winter, is hopeful "accountability" will eventually come.
He said: "For me it was about the team, Cricket Australia, coming together and saying, 'look, we didn't live up to our standards, we didn't live up to our values and three guys suffered for that'.
"I think there is a way to collectively take this still.
"Will everyone like agree on this? I can't see it happening now the way it's gotten, but for me the middle ground is the collective responsibility and accountability as a team.
"We win together, we lose together, we get caught for ball tampering, we take it together. I think that's achievable, but I can't speak for everyone."
'I got to know Bancroft really well'
Khawaja explained that he became extremely close to Bancroft on the 2019 Ashes tour of England when the latter returned to the side for the first time since 'Sandpapergate' and played what, as things currently stand, are his final two Test matches.
Bancroft's detail-filled, 4,000-word-plus account of the sandpaper deception dropped in the West Australian newspaper on the day of Australia's third ODI against in Hobart, adding even more intrigue to a story that has rocked, and gripped, cricket.
Khawaja said of his relationship with Bancroft: "In the 2019 Ashes, we both played, we got both got dropped and we would play Uno pretty much every day. If I kind of knew him at the start, I knew him really well by the end because we talked about everything.
"I remember asking him about the whole sandpaper incident once, too, He was still working his way through it at the time, trying to figure out how he's dealing with this.
"In his mind I assume he was thinking, 'I'll play 50 more games, become a legend and then I'll earn the respect back of the people'. Unfortunately it didn't work out that way for him and I think that's the thing that's really played on his mind throughout this time.
"I've kept in contact with him periodically. I remember being sat on the bus with him maybe four years ago and I brought this topic up again, asking why he didn't come out and talk about this. He said 'I can't'. He said it to me a few weeks ago actually."

items.title: Has vibe coding made open source the new normal for synths?
items.summary: The emergence of powerful vibe-coding agents and tools like Reverse Engineer Anything has caused chaos in the music gear world, leaving companies scrambling to figure out how to respond. While some, like Roland, have remained silent for now, others have embraced the modding community. In the last se
items.text:
The emergence of powerful vibe-coding agents and tools like Reverse Engineer Anything has caused chaos in the music gear world, leaving companies scrambling to figure out how to respond. While some, like Roland, have remained silent for now, others have embraced the modding community. In the last several weeks, as it’s become clear that no piece of music gear is safe from Claude and a subreddit full of curious tinkerers, companies have begun making more and more of their devices open source.
Has vibe coding made open source the new normal for synths?
Companies like Akai have decided to embrace the modding community rather than resist vibe coders.
The biggest name to decide “if you can’t beat ’em, join ’em” is inMusic, the parent company of Akai, Moog, Native Instruments, and more. “We’re going to provide a toolbox to the community, we’re going to provide the inner workings of, say, an MPC or Sample so that people can do what they want,” inMusic CEO Jack O’Donnell tells The Verge. That includes a recently launched SDK and several open-source devices, including the recently teased MPC Sample Key.
Akai is trying to walk a fine line, offering modders access while keeping its products reliable for professionals. O’Donnell says the company will “try to give them a reset button” so “they can experiment with it, and then not lose what they have.”
Behringer has also rushed to cash in, announcing a slew of open-source devices. In just a matter of weeks, it announced a $150 clone of the MPC One called Kick, a clone of the E-mu SP-1200, the Anima DJ controller, the Ignite sequencer, and the Polykeys 61 MIDI controller, all of which are open source. It’s unclear when any of these products might launch.
M-Vave’s FM-1 helped kick-start the whole movement. The $70 pocketable clone of the iconic Yamaha DX7 became the synth of the summer not just because of its dirt-cheap price and faithfully re-created ’80s tones, but because it also turned out to be infinitely hackable. There are well over a dozen different custom firmwares for the FM-1. M-Vave responded by releasing an open-source firmware with more features for developers to build on. The company also confirmed that a successor, the FM-2, is in development and will be open source as well.
Other companies have also embraced the modding community. Erica Synths recently released the source code for its LXR-02 drum machine, but founder Ģirts Ozoliņš isn’t necessarily fully on board with vibe coding. “Inventions succeed if they solve some fundamental problems, right?” he tells The Verge. “So, I’m still wondering what fundamental problem vibe coding solves.”
“We’re going to provide a toolbox to the community.”
While he can’t imagine a producer simply stacking his studio with a bunch of hacked FM-1s running various synth engines, he’s curious to see what the community cooks up for the LXR. And he does see a benefit in making music tech a little less disposable. “What I like on the upside of this is that there is some trace of sustainability. Instead of buying five or 10 plastic boxes, you can try options on one,” he says, though he’s under no illusions about the environmental impact of vibe coding. “Of course it by far does not offset data center impact on the planet and on ecology and stuff like that.”
Polyend has also gotten on board, open-sourcing its line of Tracker grooveboxes. The Polish company’s decision to open its arms to vibe coders isn’t too much of a surprise. Last year it released the Endless guitar pedal, which lets users vibe-code their own effects. Opening its other instruments to AI tinkering feels like a natural extension.
Elektron is less thrilled about the emergence of vibe-coded mods. The company banned links to custom firmware from its official forums, saying, “We would always warn against modifications to our firmware and/or machines that could brick them (potentially rendering them unusable), prevent future updates, affect warranty coverage.”
Elektron’s CPO Christian Alsing told YouTuber EZBOT that he was sympathetic to the hacker community and that the company has roots there with its first instrument, the Sidstation (based on the iconic SID sound chip from the Commodore 64). He also said that he believes users have a right to modify their devices as they see fit. But he pushed back on the idea that Elektron is “withholding features,” an accusation that Akai also faced.
Ģirts also defended Elektron, saying, “people tend to blame the company, saying they are hiding features ... you design an instrument, you have a specific concept in mind, and you cannot foresee millions of possibilities ... it’s not about hiding features; it’s more about having an idea of how an instrument should look and work.”
Other major music manufacturers, like Roland, Korg, Arturia, and Novation – all of whom did not comment for this story – have yet to issue any public statements about the explosion of AI-aided custom firmwares.

items.title: The questions Jensen Huang and Nvidia will still have to answer about Megaspeed
items.summary: Jensen Huang’s return as CEO to Nvidia hasn’t eased the scrutiny the company confronts. The chipmaker still faces multiple inquiries into allegations that its advanced GPUs were smuggled into China by a customer, the Singapore-based data center operator Megaspeed, in violation of US export rules des
items.text:
Jensen Huang’s return as CEO to Nvidia hasn’t eased the scrutiny the company confronts. The chipmaker still faces multiple inquiries into allegations that its advanced GPUs were smuggled into China by a customer, the Singapore-based data center operator Megaspeed, in violation of US export rules designed to slow China’s development of frontier AI models.
The central question for investigators is what Nvidia knew about where those chips ended up, and whether Huang’s affair with a Megaspeed executive gave the company reason to doubt Megaspeed’s assurances. Huang’s return doesn’t settle that. US Attorney General Todd Blanche has suggested Nvidia isn’t a target of an investigation, but California’s attorney general and Congress are pressing ahead, and the Securities & Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating, too.
The US government opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 and requested information from Nvidia about its billions of dollars in sales to the company, concerned that some of the chips Megaspeed bought for data center projects in Malaysia were in fact being diverted to China. Singapore also began investigating similar allegations in 2025. Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing.
Diversion of this kind would be a fairly routine issue for a company like Nvidia, whose in-demand chips are the targets of smugglers and re-sellers. When it comes to compliance and liability for export control violations, Nvidia and other chip sellers need assurances that the end users of their chips are obeying the rules. However, they also cannot ignore other information that might call the reliability of those assurances into question, export control attorneys told TechCrunch.
And that’s why Jensen Huang’s affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang was such a problem for Nvidia, likely even more so than her alleged role as a source for Chinese intelligence agencies. If Nvidia personnel, from lower-level employees up to the CEO, had reason to believe that statements from Megaspeed weren’t reliable, the attorneys said, that would increase the company’s legal risk.
“Government investigators likely would want to know, notwithstanding whatever formal assurances were exchanged between the parties, what anyone at Nvidia actually knew about the end use and end users of the chips,” Dan Fisher-Owens, an attorney at the firm Berliner Corcoran & Rowe, told TechCrunch last week.
The concern Nvidia’s board faced when it decided to oust Huang is that he knew more about what Megaspeed was doing with Nvidia’s products than was reflected in any of the compliance statements. The Wall Street Journal reported that Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, were part of a network of businesses that funneled chips to a company in Shanghai. Kang also reportedly introduced his wife to Jensen Huang, whom he had known for a decade.
On Monday, the US government added Megaspeed and its affiliates to a list of companies restricted from US trade due to national security concerns. The US also issued new rules last week barring large data centers that purchase US chips from serving customers in China and other nations seen as problematic by the US government. Nvidia, meanwhile, said it would stop selling licensed chips to China, and laid out plans to hire its first compliance officer and create a new board committee focused on export controls.
Nvidia’s board said it reinstated Huang on Monday after receiving “input from senior levels of the United States government” that left it confident his return posed no national security risk. President Donald Trump later said he called into the meeting to give them that assurance.
In a news conference Tuesday, Blanche said that Nvidia was “a good corporate citizen” and suggested it is not the target of an investigation, but Blanche declined to answer questions about the government’s investigation into Megaspeed, which the Justice Department said was ongoing as recently as last week.
“When you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don’t know what you’re talking about,” Blanche said.
Other authorities may be more demanding. Nvidia faces investigations by California Attorney General Rob Bonta and, reportedly, the SEC, both tied to its corporate disclosures. While many details of the investigation still aren’t known, short sellers complained about the company’s decision to stop breaking out its exports to Singapore in financial filings after journalists raised concerns about chip diversion.
Members of Congress from both parties say they want answers from Nvidia, with many citing alarm about China and some questioning the White House’s role in Huang’s return. Three committees in the House of Representatives will privately interview Huang and Nvidia’s top lawyer, Tim Teter, next week. Teter reportedly intervened in the Department of Commerce’s investigation of Megaspeed last year.
“We remain committed to getting answers on the mass smuggling of Nvidia products, their diversion for Chinese military purposes, and their key role in advancing our foremost adversary’s AI capabilities,” the Republican chairs of House committees focused on foreign affairs, intelligence, and China said in a joint statement.
Rep. Brian Mast, the chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, has also demanded that the Department of Commerce share extensive data regarding its investigation into chip smuggling, including by Megaspeed and its affiliates.
The Senate Banking Committee will also question Huang in a public hearing on Dec. 3.
“Mr. Huang, Nvidia executives, and the company’s board still owe Congress answers about the company’s compliance with U.S. export controls,” Senator Elizabeth Warren, the ranking Democratic member on the committee, said in a statement. “The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what ‘input’ was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement.”

items.title: ‘He’s more elegant’: Bellingham downplays Zidane comparisons after wondergoal
items.summary: “It was one of those moments when you’re just: ‘Wow.’” Bernardo Silva had a good view of Jude Bellingham scoring the goal, the golazo, that put Real Madrid into the lead and the Bernabéu on its feet, shock giving way to song, naa, naa, naa, na-na-na-naa, na-na-na-naa ringing round again. “I have no
items.text:
“It was one of those moments when you’re just: ‘Wow.’” Bernardo Silva had a good view of Jude Bellingham scoring the goal, the golazo, that put Real Madrid into the lead and the Bernabéu on its feet, shock giving way to song, naa, naa, naa, na-na-na-naa, na-na-na-naa ringing round again. “I have no idea what I did,” the Englishman said afterwards. What he did was turn all Le Tissier. Lifting the ball with his left, raising it with his right, twisting and not letting it drop, he sent it arching from the outside of his boot into the far corner, something straight out of the 90s.
“I just kind of hit it,” Bellingham reckoned; not wanting to hit it too hard, it had gone “looping”, “stabbing”, he said. “Normally they’re a lot closer, aren’t they? I was a bit surprised, honestly. Normally from there I’m looking to see who is an option to play it through to, but it popped up nicely. It was nice.” Nice? It was, Silva said, “special”. A “work of art” Marca called it. The presenter on one radio station claimed it was the best goal he had ever seen, and it wasn’t just him; wasn’t just the goal, either.
“I thought, maybe wrongly, that we could win without Bellingham,” José Mourinho admitted afterwards. The Englishman had what Madrid’s manager called an “almost injury” but at half-time, with Madrid a goal down against PSV Eindhoven and thankful it was just one, he had decided that he had to go on anyway. He had also given them what Bellingham called a “kick up the backside we needed”. Fifteen minutes later, Bellingham was standing there, arms wide. Madrid were 2-1 up; by the end it was 5-1, Bellingham setting Vinícius Júnior free for the fifth.
He had been “absolutely devastating”, Mourinho said. Some injury: everywhere and everything, he had transformed them all, Madrid growing in what El País called “the burning light of Bellingham’s sun”. Marca led on: “Jude resuscitates Real Madrid.” “Bellingham stages a festival,” said AS, Tomas Roncero calling him “the Colossus of Stourbridge”. He had been Polyphemus, El Mundo reckoned. The veteran journalist Alfredo Relano described him as the closest thing to Alfredo Di Stefano in “how he runs the game, spreading optimism to everyone”.
Then there was Zinedine Zidane, whose number he has inherited and with whom the comparisons were everywhere. During the game on Tuesday night he had “Zidaned”, Marca said and so did pretty much everyone else. After the game, the same name was put to him. “It’s a bit much that, eh,” Bellingham replied. “Zidane is much better than me, much more elegant. He is my idol.”
Actually, Bellingham has matched Zidane for leagues and Champions Leagues at Real Madrid already. And, as Jorge Valdano was swift to point out, it’s not just that he might be the best midfielder in the world right now; it’s that he’s still just 23. In theory, there’s a decade more of this; in theory, Bellingham’s prime is still to come.
Set to extend his contract to 2031 in the coming days, these are Bellingham’s best days. At the start of the season Mourinho had said: “He’s a No 10. He can’t play … well, he can play as a 6 or an 8, but then you lose him being closer to goal and I like that Jude.” Yet while there has been a shift this can still feel like the Jude that is everywhere too, the kid who was once handed the No 22 shirt because he was a 10, and 8 and a 4 all together, a player who can’t be stopped as he strides towards the area, opponents flying off him when he turns, like a catherine wheel spinning through midfield.
“He’s very special,” Silva told TNT. “He is a player that can create something very different at any moment like today. Physically he is very strong, the way he keeps the ball, the way he allows us to attack, the way he drives with the ball. He is good at everything. He is a complete player.”
Mourinho described him as “an extraordinary player”. He said: “Jude has everything: the physique, the technical ability, the understanding of the play, vision … everything. He is the best midfielder in the world. He changed the game. He is a natural leader, he makes huge demands of himself: you see that every day in the way he trains. He doesn’t hide his frustration when things don’t go well but he combats that with work, by putting the machine to work.”
Unleashed and undroppable, he has seven goals and five assists, as if it is even about that, however absurd the latest one was. Few, if any, footballers are playing better anywhere. Even if asked about the Ballon d’Or – yes, already – Bellingham replied that he doesn’t care about that, claiming that’s a journalists’ thing.
“I have a bit more experience now: there’s the coach, the staff, the confidence I have from the World Cup,” he said, speaking to the media in English and Spanish. “My Spanish is getting better, although I get a bit nervous with you. It’s easier in the changing room where I can say bad words. I’m loving it here. For English players, it’s such a good thing to play abroad.”

items.title: Israeli MPs advance bill for inquiry into security failings that led to October 7 Hamas attack
items.summary:
Israeli MPs advance bill for inquiry into security failings that led to October 7 Hamas attack
Israeli MPs on Wednesday gave their initial approval for the creation of a commission to investigate the security failures that led to the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas. Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin
items.text:
Israeli MPs advance bill for inquiry into security failings that led to October 7 Hamas attack
Israeli MPs on Wednesday gave their initial approval for the creation of a commission to investigate the security failures that led to the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas. Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was in power when the attack happened, has repeatedly rejected calls to set up such a probe.
Israeli lawmakers on Wednesday gave initial approval for a bill to create a state commission of inquiry into the security failures that led to Hamas's unprecedented October 7, 2023 attack.
In a preliminary reading, 65 members of parliament voted in favour and 50 against the bill put forward by a lawmaker from the party of prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot.
On the election campaign trail, Eisenkot had pledged to swiftly establish an independent state commission into the failures that allowed Hamas's attack which resulted in the deaths of more than 1,200 people.
Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government, which was in office when the attack occurred, has rejected calls to set up such a probe and instead proposed a bipartisan commission whose members would be appointed by politicians.
The bill will now head to a committee in the Knesset, Israel's parliament, and have to pass through three further readings before becoming law.
A statement from the Knesset detailing the bill said that the commission would consist of five members and would be required to publish an interim report within one year of the announcement of its establishment.
The bill allocates a budget of seven million shekels (about $2 million) for the commission's creation.
Eisenkot's Yashar party described the legislation as "essential to uncovering the truth and drawing the lessons needed to safeguard Israel's security".
Many Israelis have demanded an independent probe into the deadliest day in the country's history, which inflicted a profound national trauma whose repercussions continue to be felt.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

items.text:
Trump to meet Abdul El-Sayed: Will he agree to a renamed Medicare-for-all?
After offer to rename policy ‘TrumpCare’, US president calls Democratic victor ‘a smart guy’ weeks after a bitter Senate race in Michigan.
United States President Donald Trump says he will meet Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed to discuss the Democrat’s push for a single, low-cost government health insurance programme, which El-Sayed has suggested renaming “Trumpcare”.
One month ago, Trump was using anti-Muslim rhetoric against El-Sayed during his race against Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan.
But on Tuesday, the US president appeared to have changed his tune. During a 45-minute interview in the Oval Office, he told the New York Post, “He’s a smart guy,” as he answered questions about El-Sayed’s offer to rename “Medicare for All” as “Trumpcare”.
“He did a good job. He actually did a very good job,” the president said.
“I know I’ll be meeting with him,” he added. “Maybe there’s some place in the middle that we could go.” He did not give a date for the meeting.
Since the Republicans’ crushing defeat in the November 3 midterm elections, in which they lost their majorities in the US Senate and the House of Representatives, Trump has already indicated that he plans to make liberal use of his presidential veto to block “insane” Democratic policies.
However, he has also suggested that he may be open to negotiations, telling Fox News that he would “veto, veto, veto” but the Democrats would eventually call him hoping to do a deal.
“Congratulations to the Democrats. They did a good job,” Trump said. “I congratulate them and look forward to working with them for the good of our country.”
Here is what we know:
What has El-Sayed proposed, and how has Trump responded?
In the New York Post interview, Trump praised El-Sayed’s idea of putting his name on the healthcare programme as “very smart”. He also said he and Democrats could work together on healthcare but “Obamacare hasn’t worked”.
Obamacare was an overhaul of the individual health insurance market under former President Barack Obama that had slowed increases in insurance costs and halved the number of uninsured Americans.
Trump added: “I’m just going to veto everything there is, and then at some point, I think they’re going to want to negotiate.”
El-Sayed first floated the idea of renaming the proposed healthcare plan on November 6 in an interview with Zeteo editor-in-chief Mehdi Hasan. “If he wants to pass Trumpcare for all, I’m OK with it. He seems to like to put his name on things,” El-Sayed said.
On November 12, he posted a mock-up of a gold “TrumpCare” insurance card bearing the president’s signature on X. “Donald, this is on the table,” he wrote. “Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave.”
In a video posted on November 17, El-Sayed addressed the president as “habibi”, an Arabic term of affection. “Trumpcare for all. It’s really popular. People really want healthcare,” he said. “You can put your name all over it.”
The White House was initially dismissive. Spokesperson Allison Schuster called the proposal “Medicare for none” and described it as a socialist government takeover of healthcare.
But on Saturday, Trump reshared El-Sayed’s post on his Truth Social platform without comment. NBC News later reported that Vice President JD Vance’s office had contacted El-Sayed’s team to set up a meeting.
On the NBC TV network’s Meet the Press programme the next day, El-Sayed called the plan “the ultimate Trump card”. He said he did not care what it was called as long as universal healthcare coverage passed. In a post on Monday, he wrote: “The point of winning elections is to do something good with the seat.”
What did Trump previously say about El-Sayed?
The warmth displayed by the president is a reversal of his previous approach to El-Sayed.
During the election campaign, Trump repeatedly questioned El-Sayed’s loyalty to the US and tried to tie him to the Muslim Brotherhood.
At an October 25 rally in Port Huron, Michigan, Trump said he was there “to keep a jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator”. There is no evidence that El-Sayed has any affiliation with the group, and he has denied any. Democrats denounced the attacks as targeting El-Sayed’s faith and his Egyptian heritage.
Vance told a rally in August that there was “something about Abdul El-Sayed that is very, very evil”.
El-Sayed, a physician and former head of Detroit’s Health Department, hit back throughout the campaign and at one point called Trump an “unserious fool”. He defeated Rogers to become the first Muslim member of the US Senate.
How is healthcare paid for in the US?
While most other wealthy countries have built universal health systems paid for from taxes, the US has relied largely on voluntary private insurance, leaving a substantial share of the population without coverage.
Despite decades of calls for national public insurance, it was not until 1965 that Washington created its two main public programmes: Medicare for people aged 65 and older, and Medicaid for people on low incomes.
Medicare, which also covers some younger people with disabilities, now serves nearly 70 million people.
Most Americans under 65 with health insurance rely on a patchwork of employer-provided insurance; private plans bought through the Obamacare, or Affordable Care Act, marketplaces; and Medicaid.
According to the US Census Bureau, 26.7 million people, or 7.9 percent of the population, were uninsured for all of 2025.
The Affordable Care Act, passed in 2010, made almost all lawfully present residents eligible for more affordable coverage than they had before. But taking it up remains largely voluntary, and millions still go without insurance, often citing cost as the barrier.

items.summary:
Trinity Rodman out of USWNT’s World Cup qualifier due to shoulder injury
Star forward Trinity Rodman sustained a minor shoulder injury during Washington Spirit’s 2-1 loss to Kansas City.
Trinity Rodman has not been included in the United States women’s national team squad for a qualifying tournament
items.text:
Trinity Rodman out of USWNT’s World Cup qualifier due to shoulder injury
Star forward Trinity Rodman sustained a minor shoulder injury during Washington Spirit’s 2-1 loss to Kansas City.
Trinity Rodman has not been included in the United States women’s national team squad for a qualifying tournament for the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 because of a minor shoulder injury.
Rodman, 24, was injured on Saturday early in the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current in the NWSL Championship Game — the Spirit’s third consecutive setback in the title match.
She was challenging for a ball when Current defender Laney Rouse collided with her midair and sent Rodman hard to the ground. Rodman left the playing field for several minutes and met with trainers before returning to the game.
Gotham FC midfielder Jaedyn Shaw has replaced Rodman on the 23-player roster for the CONCACAF W Championship tournament, which is a qualifier for the Women’s World Cup next summer in Brazil.
The USA squad opens the tournament on Friday against El Salvador in the quarterfinals in Mansfield, Texas. Eight teams are competing, with the four quarterfinal winners clinching the confederation’s four direct World Cup spots. Jamaica opens with Costa Rica, Canada plays Panama, and Mexico faces Haiti this weekend.
A victory for the Americans would send them to the semifinals on December 1, also at Texas Health Mansfield Stadium. The championship is slated for December 5 in Houston. The tournament also determines the region’s squads for the 2028 Olympics.
Rodman recorded 15 goals and 10 assists in a total of 33 games for the Spirit this season.
Shaw, who turned 22 on Friday, helped Gotham FC capture the NWSL Shield as the league’s regular-season champion. She scored 11 regular-season goals.

items.text:
Raheem Sterling - from national icon to suspended jail sentence
- Published
Raheem Sterling grew up a stone's throw from Wembley Stadium, and went on to start a European Championship final for England there.
At his peak, the four-time Premier League winner was earning £325,000 a week at Chelsea.
"Raheem is a huge player with a huge influence in the last few years in English football," said then Blues boss Thomas Tuchel when he signed a 27-year-old Sterling in a £50m deal in 2022.
"He is at the perfect age to take responsibility around the younger players that we have and be an example.
"He just needs to do what he did over the last few years and he will be a huge asset for us."
Sterling enjoyed a 10-year England career, also played for Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal, and commanded combined transfer fees of about £100m.
But his career at the top level looks to be in the balance at the age of 31 after he was handed a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, for dangerous driving. Sterling has also been disqualified from driving for two years and ordered to carry out 100 hours of unpaid work.
At an earlier hearing in September, Sterling admitted dangerous driving on a motorway before crashing a Lamborghini on 28 May.
The crash caused "substantial" damage to his car and all four wheels, which prevented him from driving further, the court heard.
Sterling also admitted possessing nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, and failing to provide a specimen for analysis.
A stark warning aged 10
Sterling's life was touched by tragedy at a young age.
Born in Kingston, Jamaica, he was just two when his father was shot dead.
His mother, Nadine, was determined to give her children a safer environment to live in. She moved to England to lay a path for Sterling and his sister to join her once she had found a home and finished her education, while cleaning bathrooms and changing bedsheets in hotels to earn extra money.
Sterling grew up on a housing estate in Neasden, north-west London, and spent part of his education at Vernon House, where teachers attempted to help the football-obsessed youngster with behavioural problems.
In an interview with the Players' Tribune, external in 2018, Sterling said: "I was so naughty that they kicked me out of primary school. I just didn't like to listen to anyone but my mum. That was my problem."
He was 10 when teacher Chris Beschi told him: "If you carry on the way you're going, by the time you're 17 you'll either be playing for England or in prison."
Sterling would grow to become one of the standout English attacking talents of his generation.
- Raheem Sterling: From school struggles to a class of his own 
  - Published14 November 2012
On 14 November 2012 - aged 17 years and 342 days - Sterling made his England debut on the night his Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard won his 100th cap in a 4-2 defeat by Sweden in Stockholm.
Sterling would go on to make 81 more appearances for his country, scoring 20 goals.
He featured at three World Cups - 2014, 2018 and 2022 - and two European Championships. He was one of the standout players as England reached the Euro 2020 final at Wembley, where they were beaten by Italy.
Sterling was now at the peak of his career - the former Queens Park Rangers youngster, who has a tattoo on his forearm of a young boy holding a football looking up at the Wembley arch, named in the team of the tournament by Uefa.
Liverpool had signed a 15-year-old Sterling from QPR for £600,000 in February 2010.
He made his senior Reds debut two years later and became the second-youngest goalscorer in their history - behind Michael Owen - when he scored the winner against Reading in October 2012 at the age of 17.
In 2015, Sterling joined Manchester City in a deal worth up to £49m, making him the most expensive English player at the time.
He had been under contract at Anfield until 2017 but turned down a new deal to move to Liverpool's rivals, with City boss Manuel Pellegrini describing the 20-year-old as "one of the best attacking players in world football".
Sterling went on to score 131 goals in 339 appearances in all competitions during seven successful years at Etihad Stadium.
As well as four Premier League titles, he helped City win five League Cups, one FA Cup and one Community Shield.
It was while he was at City, in 2021, that Sterling became an MBE in the Queen's Birthday Honours for his services to racial equality in sport.
"I am grateful to have been recognised," he said. "But my priority is to try to help to educate society and myself. I'm learning every day."
After City came the move to Chelsea, where his career began to stall.
Tuchel, now England manager, was sacked two months after signing Sterling, who made just 45 Premier League starts for the Blues over four years.
Off the pitch, he launched a scholarship fund aimed at closing the gap in the number of black British students who go to university.
On the pitch, he was finding it a struggle.
He spent 18 months as a member of Chelsea's so-called 'bomb squad', and a season-long loan to Arsenal in 2024-25 proved largely unsuccessful.
- 'Sterling will look back and wonder' 
  - Published17 April 2015
Making headlines off the pitch
As well as his success on the field, Sterling has made headlines off it too.
In 2015, when he was 20, reports began to surface about his behaviour away from the game.
Sterling was pictured apparently inhaling nitrous oxide and was also photographed smoking a shisha pipe.
That prompted then Liverpool boss Brendan Rodgers to warn Sterling he would "look back in 20 years and wonder what he was doing".
Sterling also made headlines while on duty for England at the 2018 World Cup in Russia.
The Sun ran a story titled "Raheem shoots himself in the foot" as pictures emerged of a tattoo of an M16 assault rifle on his leg.
