items.title: Rayan Cherki magic denies Napoli but Manchester City’s struggles continue
items.summary: This was the perfect snapshot of Manchester City’s autumn difficulties. They simply cannot keep the door shut and looked like being picked off by Napoli, who had scored through Rasmus Højlund and Noa Lang either side of Ayyoub Bouaddi’s equaliser. Then Rayan Cherki, insistent but frustrated for most
items.text:
This was the perfect snapshot of Manchester City’s autumn difficulties. They simply cannot keep the door shut and looked like being picked off by Napoli, who had scored through Rasmus Højlund and Noa Lang either side of Ayyoub Bouaddi’s equaliser. Then Rayan Cherki, insistent but frustrated for most of the evening, seized the mantle five minutes from time and earned a welcome but deeply flawed draw. It meant Kevin De Bruyne, whose return last season had been ill-starred, was denied a deserved victory on his old home turf.
The buildup was largely a homage to De Bruyne, who was serenaded at the end of the warm-up and cheered upon the announcement of his name. It had all been done 14 months previously too, although back then De Bruyne lasted only 26 minutes, when a red card to Giovanni Di Lorenzo brought his sacrifice and an eventual 2-0 defeat. There have been few like the Belgian and his latest return was a luscious reminder, in these heavily asterisked times, of garlands collected under the same grim cloud.
In truth neither City nor a creaky Napoli, who are eighth in Serie A and functional rather than flowing, are the alluring propositions of days past. Beyond the De Bruyne appreciation ritual and a vocal performance from the visitors’ upper-tier contingent, this latest procedural wedge of league phase content commenced to near silence. City’s emergence in a new all-orange kit, apparently earmarked for selected Champions League games and timed handily for the festive season, added a degree of visual warmth to the late November chill.
Maresca needs his own tenure, stuttering amid selection uncertainties and questions over the team’s balance as well as the looming elephant, to catch light. Within a minute of kick-off Elliot Anderson came close to providing the spark with a low 20-yarder that Vanja Milinkovic-Savic parried unconvincingly. Anderson, scorer of a superb volley in Saturday’s otherwise laboured draw with Fulham, had kept his place in a side showing five changes.
City threatened again when Nico O’Reilly headed over at the far post and, even though Josko Gvardiol needed sound timing to stop a marauding Matteo Politano down the right, it was clear enough Napoli’s menace would not exceed the sporadic. As the half-hour approached Højlund shot tamely at Gianluigi Donnarumma from an angle but the concern for a ponderous City was that, since those early exchanges, they had shown little suggestion of conjuring a breakthrough. A considered ball in from Anderson, missed by a karate-kicking Erling Haaland, offered thin gruel.
Anderson sought Haaland again with a delivery that was shovelled behind for a corner. Napoli had hardly oozed composure but City’s speed of thought and movement had been too slow. When De Bruyne, manning the midfield alongside Scott McTominay and Billy Gilmour, fumbled possession inside his own half the hosts lacked sufficient zip to take advantage.
Haaland made contact with a Cherki cross but his header looped into the arms of Milinkovic-Savic. City had, at least, shown they could locate him. Shortly before half-time Napoli, firmly in the game, offered a precious glimmer of excitement when Sam Beukema’s header from a corner was batted away smartly by Donnarumma.
Napoli brought the first palpitations of the second half, too, when Lang briefly seemed to get in behind before O’Reilly recovered to stall his run. At the other end McTominay blocked from Cherki, atoning after his wild slash at the same player had put Napoli under some pressure. City had lacked width and wit all night so it was no surprise to see Jérémy Doku readying himself five minutes after the restart.
Doku arrived soon enough, replacing the anonymous Allan, but was turning away in despair within 30 seconds. This time Højlund’s bearings were perfect after taking a Gilmour pass and taking the ball outside a flailing Marc Guéhi, the finish cut sharply across Donnarumma and fizzed low into his left corner. Napoli had, to their credit, visibly upped things in the preceding spell.
Would City now do the same? Next cab off the rank was Iliman Ndiaye, with Enzo Fernández making way after a featureless showing. The slightest uptick in tempo and intent brought dividends. Doku had just slipped Anderson in for a shot well saved by Milinkovic-Savic when, from the resulting short corner, he was allowed to tee up Bouaddi 14 yards out.
The finish was swept in confidently and, given City’s previous toils, all too simply.
At last City had momentum, although the crowd’s newly discovered enthusiasm was channelled back towards De Bruyne when he was replaced in the 75th minute. Perhaps that interlude helped reverse the swelling tide. Immediately Leonardo Spinazzola, given acres down the right, crossed beyond the far post for Lang to volley in thrillingly.
City were spluttering again but Cherki, surging into a shooting position inside the box, crashed a fine strike past Milinkovic-Savic to secure parity.

items.title: Dortmund’s Beier halts Arsenal charge after thunderbolt from Gyökeres
items.summary: Arsenal’s sky-high standards are slipping. For the second time in four days, Mikel Arteta’s side found themselves a goal up at half-time and apparently cruising towards victory, only for their opponents to rouse themselves and earn a deserved draw. After Newcastle on Saturday, this time it was an im
items.text:
Arsenal’s sky-high standards are slipping. For the second time in four days, Mikel Arteta’s side found themselves a goal up at half-time and apparently cruising towards victory, only for their opponents to rouse themselves and earn a deserved draw. After Newcastle on Saturday, this time it was an impressive Borussia Dortmund who became only the second side to take points off Arsenal in their past 15 group stage games in this competition.
It could have been worse had an offside flag not ruled out Jobe Bellingham’s goal after Max Beier equalised a thunderbolt from Viktor Gyökeres. But the much-maligned Sweden striker was guilty of a glaring miss late on as Arsenal laid siege to Dortmund’s goal, with the German side having to hang on for a result that gave their travelling fans a night to remember. A frustrated Arteta will know his side must be more clinical when Real Madrid and Jude Bellingham visit north London in a fortnight.
While Max Dowman and Ethan Nwaneri – on loan at Dortmund from the Gunners – had to make do with a place on their respective benches, the exploits of another teenager were on the Arsenal supporters’ lips on their way to the ground. A stunning solo goal from 14-year-old Luis Muñoz – an England Under-15 international who is the youngest player ever to feature in the Uefa Youth League – against Dortmund earlier in the day showed that Arsenal’s conveyor belt of talent continues to produce.
Aside from Myles Lewis-Skelly – a relative veteran these days at 20 – Arteta opted for experience as he made six changes from the draw against Newcastle on Saturday, including Kepa Arrizabalaga deputising in goal for the injured David Raya.
Dortmund haven’t been crowned German champions since Jürgen Klopp’s days in 2012 but lead the Bundesliga by two points from Bayern Munich. Like Arsenal, Niko Kovac’s side has relied on a solid defence and the Croatian manager attempted to stiffen his midfield by selecting Joey Veerman alongside Jobe Bellingham and ahead of their exciting Greece teenager, Konstantinos Karetsas.
Arrizabalaga had only started once this season, in the Carabao Cup win over Ipswich, and the Spain goalkeeper was largely a spectator again for the first 20 minutes as Arsenal assumed control. Christos Tzolis had two early sighters after being set up by the rejuvenated Noni Madueke but the Dortmund goalkeeper, Gregor Kobel, still seemed surprised by the power with which Gyökeres struck the ball in the 10th minute when he was fed by the England forward.
He was only introduced in the fourth minute of stoppage time against Newcastle as Arsenal chased a winner but scored an excellent goal in the victory over Slavia Prague three weeks ago and clearly had a point to prove as his shot arrowed into the back of the net from outside the area.
Kobel managed to get a hand to a Tzolis effort that was heading for the top corner soon after, although Madueke should really have doubled Arsenal’s lead on the rebound. Dortmund eventually managed to create some pressure at the other end when Fábio Silva fired over. But despite the best efforts of Bellingham and Felix Nmecha, they just could not sustain any meaningful possession against the dominance of Declan Rice and Lewis-Skelly.
A marauding run from the latter straight through the heart of Dortmund’s defence almost resulted in a second after a brilliant touch from Gyökeres. You began to wonder if Arsenal’s profligacy might cost them again when Arrizabalaga was finally called into action on the stroke of half-time after a rare mistake from Rice but he managed to push Julian Ryerson’s shot out for a corner.
Arteta had more cause for concern at the start of the second half when the Dortmund supporters behind Arsenal’s goal thought they should have had a penalty after a corner struck Gyökeres on the wrist but the Italian referee waved away their protests. There were groans at the other end when Martin Ødegaard passed up the opportunity to shoot after more good work from Madueke.
That was made to look even more costly when Dortmund equalised with their next attack. The outstanding Joane Gadou stepped out of defence brilliantly to play in Beier and he made no mistake with his left foot. Piero Hincapié then saw his header saved at the near post by Kobel. Clearly fancying his chances of a shock victory, Kovac threw on Karetsas and Serhou Guirassy as Arteta made a triple substitution. But Jurriën Timber’s first act was to give the ball away, with Bellingham only denied moments later by the assistant’s flag.
The Dortmund goal led a charmed life in the final 20 minutes as Arsenal piled on the pressure. Only Guirassy will know how the ball managed to strike the post twice in the space of a second as he attempted to clear from a clever Ødegaard free-kick. Rice couldn’t believe his luck when his effort struck the post again with Kobel well beaten. But Dortmund stuck to their task admirably and Arsenal had to learn the hard way again.

items.title: Pochettino criticises Premier League officiating after Yoro red card overturned
items.summary:
Mauricio Pochettino has criticised officiating in English football, saying: “We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be in the level to drive [it],” after Leny Yoro’s Anfield red card was overturned on Tuesday.
Despite the Football Association ruling the Frenchman’s early sending-off in Sunday’s
items.text:
Mauricio Pochettino has criticised officiating in English football, saying: “We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be in the level to drive [it],” after Leny Yoro’s Anfield red card was overturned on Tuesday.
Despite the Football Association ruling the Frenchman’s early sending-off in Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool was “wrongful dismissal”, Manchester United remain furious at the decision, and at Pro Ref, the elite officials’ organisation.
Dominik Szoboszlai scored the subsequent free-kick which put Liverpool on the road to victory, and United were dismayed by Howard Webb, the Pro Ref chief, saying he could understand why Sam Barrott gave the red card and the video assistant referees backed the decision.
United remain insistent that Alexander Isak would not have reached the ball before their goalkeeper, Senne Lammens, as he was brought down by Yoro and they argue this can be objectively proved. The club also believe there was an error of process as the recording of the video officials shows a quick look at the incident with no due consideration and they have confirmed they will raise this with the Premier League and Pro Ref.
When asked about this, Pochettino also claimed Szoboszlai’s strike should not have stood as Bradley Barcola touched United’s wall. The head coach said: “We didn’t pay attention, but Bruno [Fernandes] was aware: no one talked about that the goal wasn’t legal. Should disallow the goal because Barcola was touching our wall, and maybe in the last two years maybe they changed the rule. Very disappointed because I think this type of thing never can happen.
“My question always was the same: OK, we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotional relationship [the heat of moment] within the game.
“But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? Because now, are we going to repeat the game? We need to take the time to review the situation. We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be at the level to drive [it]. We need to drive in the best way.
“We love the technology, yes? We accept that the technology is there, yes? [So] what are they doing?”
Pochettino also referenced Erling Haaland’s winner in Manchester City’s 1-0 win at United in September. Pro Ref later admitted it should not have been allowed after the video assistant referee ruled Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in the buildup.
“It’s not only this mistake or the mistake against Haaland in Manchester City when I was a spectator. It’s how after it affects everything. I need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce and to say, yes, we were right, or the decision wasn’t good. And now, where are the three points? It’s a thing that we need to think a little bit more deep.”
Speaking before the card was rescinded, Webb said: “Isak’s got control of the ball, knocks it past Yoro. He’s moving at pace and a foul comes and knocks him down. There’s a question mark around whether or not he would get on to that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would. The VAR checks to see whether that decision was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion it wasn’t.
“Most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but it’s debatable. [It’s] certainly not clearly wrong.”
The Liverpool defeat came in Pochettino’s first match as the United head coach. His side are next at Sporting in Wednesday’s fifth Champions League group game, having suffered a 4-1 humiliation at Como in the previous one under Michael Carrick. Despite this and Sunday’s reverse, which left United second-bottom in the Premier League, Pochettino was bullish when asked about the comments of Paulo Fonseca, the Sporting coach, who dismissed any notion that the visitors are fragile.
He said: “What I found is that people [outside] want it to look like we’re fragile. I don’t say that we are fragile. We are strong, we have great mentality. There are things we need to improve, of course, many things that we need to improve, but it’s normal when you are in a position that we are in the Premier League.
“We are a strong team – they showed that last season, capable of finishing third.”
Fernandes, whose contract expires in the summer, has said discussions regarding new terms are paused because of the club’s predicament. If results improve, this may allow a fresh deal for the captain to be signed.

items.title: Leaked FIFA documents show 96-year plan for stakes in WC selloff
items.summary:
NEW YORK -- Gianni Infantino 's failed private equity plan that started the biggest crisis of his FIFA presidency intended to sell stakes in the FIFA World Cup for 96 years.
Documents exchanged between FIFA and investor Joshua Kushner's firm Thrive Capital, reviewed Tuesday by The Associated Press,
items.text:
NEW YORK -- Gianni Infantino 's failed private equity plan that started the biggest crisis of his FIFA presidency intended to sell stakes in the FIFA World Cup for 96 years.
Documents exchanged between FIFA and investor Joshua Kushner's firm Thrive Capital, reviewed Tuesday by The Associated Press, also show the planned $20 billion FIFA Forward Enterprises subsidiary could have paid tens of millions of dollars in management bonuses to its executives.
The leaked documents show how the FFE deal was moving toward completion in New York on the weekend of the July 19 final of the men's World Cup.
The secretive project came to light nine days after Spain's win over Argentina in the final and the global backlash, including from senior FIFA executives, pushed Infantino to withdraw the proposal within days.
The leaked documents, including a FIFA in-house risk assessment, show its own finance officials "were not directly privy to the construction of this transaction."
"This deal provides for Fifa to create a for-profit subsidiary which would have all the commercial rights for FIFA events transferred to it for commercial exploitation for the next 96 years," the risk assessment states.
Infantino now faces a first presidential election challenge since he was elected in 2016, with two opponents campaigning ahead of a March 18 vote in Morocco: Philippe Diallo of France and Kohzo Tashima of Japan. Infantino is widely expected to be elected for another term.
The FFE private equity plan reignited concerns in Europe and Japan about Infantino's leadership style and political ties to U.S. President Donald Trump, over creating a FIFA peace prize and waiving a mandatory one-game ban at the World Cup for United States forward Folarin Balogun.
The leaked documents show FIFA was in talks with the Affinity Partners investment firm of Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, before settling on his younger brother Joshua's firm Thrive Capital as anchor investor.
Affinity Partners was cited in one document which explained why FIFA did not open a tender process "owing to the specific and unique nature of the proposed investment, bilateral and unilateral conversations held with interest from several potential investment sources."
Thrive created a "Backstop Letter and Transaction Terms" document dated July 17 about the plan with FIFA called "Project Box."
The document detailed a "Management Incentive Plan" with bonuses to be decided by the FFE board chaired by the sitting president, Infantino.
"This is customary for proposed structures of this nature," FIFA said in a statement about the project, which it had repeatedly said was a proposal needing to be approved by its 211 member federations. They effectively own FIFA as a Switzerland-based non-profit.
"FIFA's leadership would only have had leading roles in the board, which would not have led to any additional remuneration," the world soccer body said.
The leaked documents were first reported Monday by the New York Post.
European soccer body UEFA has been seeking access to FIFA's documents about the proposed selloff and were recently handed a win in Manhattan when a judge denied a FIFA request to block their release.
UEFA filed court documents in August as part of wider strategy to remove Infantino as FIFA president, which includes a potential criminal complaint against him personally in Switzerland for alleged financial mismanagement.
Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

items.title: Sources: Man United to raise concerns after refs' chief backs Yoro red card
items.summary:
LISBON, Portugal -- Manchester United are set to raise concerns with the Premier League and Pro Ref after referee's chief Howard Webb backed the decision to send off Leny Yoro against Liverpool despite the Football Association overturning the Frenchman's suspension, sources told ESPN.
United were in
items.text:
LISBON, Portugal -- Manchester United are set to raise concerns with the Premier League and Pro Ref after referee's chief Howard Webb backed the decision to send off Leny Yoro against Liverpool despite the Football Association overturning the Frenchman's suspension, sources told ESPN.
United were informed on Tuesday that Yoro's red card in the 4-0 defeat at Anfield has been rescinded after the FA upheld an appeal on the grounds of wrongful dismissal.
But it was followed hours later by Webb -- speaking on Match Officials Mic'd Up -- backing the decision made by on-field referee Sam Barrott and verified by VAR John Brooks.
Sources have told ESPN that United believe it can be proved with data that Liverpool striker Alexander Isak would not have had the chance to shoot before Senne Lammens collected the ball and therefore Yoro did not prevent a clear goalscoring opportunity.
The club, who now intend to contact the Premier League and referee's body Pro Ref directly, are also disappointed Brooks did not do more to challenge Barrott's decision and believe they have been the victim of a "process error," sources added.
Speaking at a news conference in Lisbon on Tuesday, head coach Mauricio Pochettino said: "Very disappointed because I think this type of thing never can happen.
"My question always was the same. We can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotional relationship with the game from the referee, sometimes the view, the position, obviously can be affected.
"But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? Are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play the game with similar tools? 11 by 11? No, the problem is when we were there, and in the moment that I think we need to be or take the time to review the situation.
"We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be in the level to drive. You know, we need to drive in the best way. We love the technology, yes. We accept that the technology is there, yes. What are they doing?"
United are aiming to bounce back from the heavy defeat at Anfield when they face Sporting CP in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Pochettino is looking for his first win as head coach after taking over from Michael Carrick and urged his players to "move on" from the perceived injustice against Liverpool.
It's five years since United won away from home in the Champions League, with both of their victories this season -- against Ipswich Town and Sabah FK -- having come at Old Trafford.
"You ask me a question and I need to defend our situation and our club and our players, of course," Pochettino said.
"Now move on. Now we are thinking tomorrow [against Sporting]. After the game we all were very disappointed.
"But what I felt in the dressing room is a group of players that really care, that really want to perform, that are going to do everything for the club and to change that dynamic. And of course, we need that impartial situation, you know, but when this type of situation is completely unfair, I think it's very bad.
"The thing is now they move on, we move on. We all move on in the club, all move on to try tomorrow. Tomorrow is a different competition and try to perform, and I think I am sure that tomorrow we are going to be ready to perform."

items.title: Poch fumes at Yoro red and thinks Szoboszlai goal shouldn't have stood
items.summary:
Mauricio Pochettino: Man Utd boss fumes at VAR in Liverpool loss over Leny Yoro and Dominik Szoboszlai calls
Man Utd to contact ProRef and the Premier League over 'totally wrong' interpretation of Leny Yoro's red card in loss at Liverpool after call was overturned; Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino:
items.text:
Mauricio Pochettino: Man Utd boss fumes at VAR in Liverpool loss over Leny Yoro and Dominik Szoboszlai calls
Man Utd to contact ProRef and the Premier League over 'totally wrong' interpretation of Leny Yoro's red card in loss at Liverpool after call was overturned; Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino: "What were VAR doing?"; Poch also believes Dominik Szoboszlai’s opener should not have stood
Tuesday 24 November 2026 22:05, UK
Mauricio Pochettino has heavily criticised VAR in Manchester United's loss at Liverpool after Leny Yoro's red card was overturned, while the Argentine believes Dominik Szoboszlai’s opener should not have stood.
Yoro's one-match suspension for the red card he was shown in the 4-0 defeat at Anfield has been removed, despite referees' chief Howard Webb supporting the decision to send him off.
Man Utd will contact ProRef and the Premier League directly over what they believe to be a 'totally wrong' interpretation of Yoro's red card against Liverpool.
- Man Utd to contact PL and refs over 'totally wrong' Yoro red card
- Man Utd news & transfers🔴 | Man Utd fixtures & scores
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- No Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract📺
It is the second time this season VAR has wrongly gone against Man Utd after ProRef admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford in September.
United received an apology over the incorrect VAR decision to award Erling Haaland's winner, which was initially ruled offside before VAR overturned the decision.
Pochettino mentioned the Haaland call in a passionate outburst over VAR as he questioned why the VAR did not intervene to overturn the on-field decision.
Speaking at a press conference ahead of his team's Champions League match against Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday, Pochettino said: "Very disappointed because I think this type of thing never can happen.
"My question was always the same - we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotional relationship with the game.
"But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? No, because now we are going to repeat the game? We're going to have the possibility to play with the similar tools, 11 against 11?
"The problem is that when we were there, I think they need to take their time to review the situation.
"We have an unbelievable car but we need to be in the level to drive, we need to drive in the best way.
"We love and accept the technology, but what are they doing? But it's not only this mistake or the mistake for Haaland against Manchester City, it's how after it affects everything."
Poch explains why Szoboszlai goal shouldn't have stood
Pochettino then insisted that Liverpool's opening goal should not have stood because Bradley Barcola was touching the Manchester United wall as Szoboszlai struck in.
Pochettino referenced a similar call last season, which saw Eberechi Eze's free-kick goal for Crystal Palace at Chelsea disallowed after ex-Palace captain Marc Guehi pushed Moises Caicedo to create a gap for the ball to fly through.
The IFAB Laws of the Game state: "If, when a free-kick is taken, an attacking team player is less than 1 m (1 yd) from a 'wall' formed by three or more defending team players, an indirect free-kick is awarded."
Pochettino believes that the law applied to Szoboszlai's free-kick opener due to Barcola's involvement.
He said: "No one talks about that the goal wasn't legal, it should be disallowed because (Bradley) Barcola was touching our wall. Maybe in the last two years, they've maybe changed the rule because I've been in America, but last season when (Eberechi) Eze scored for Palace (at Chelsea) you can see [it was disallowed].
"But VAR didn't check [Dominik Szoboszlai's goal]; that must be disallowed.
"But this type of situation, I need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce and to say we were right and the decision wasn't good, and now the three points, where are they?
"I think it's a thing we need to think a little bit more deeper and it's not for tomorrow's game.
"It's about to be tough in the way we use the technology. We need to move on. I'm so proud of the players in the way they manage these unfair situations that happen on the field.
"Our focus now is to improve, to start to win games and tomorrow we have a great opportunity here."
What did Webb say about Yoro decision?
In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'd Up, Webb, chief refereeing officer at ProRef, described the on-field decision from referee Samuel Barrott as "decisive" and said the point of contention was around whether Isak would beat United goalkeeper Senne Lammens to the ball.
Audio from the officials reveals that the VAR, John Brooks, who backed Barrott's decision, determined Isak was "likely" to get on the end of the ball before Lammens. His assistant VAR, Paul Howard, agreed.
Webb was non-committal in his verdict but backed the process of the officials by saying "most people would see that as a correct decision".
"There's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens," said Webb. "Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would. That was the referee's call made on the field.
"The VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect and formed the opinion that it wasn't. If there was any doubt, then it was doubt.
"It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. And I think by and large most people would see that as a correct decision with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.
"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong."

items.title: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy
items.summary:
After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man.
Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. During that meeting, CNBC reported
items.text:
After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man.
Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. During that meeting, CNBC reported that Huang struck a “remorseful tone” and told the crowd “I hurt all of you.”
The founder, whose extramarital affairs have been accused of jeopardizing everything from the stock market to U.S. national security, went on to describe how difficult the current moment is for him: “This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang reportedly told staff.
“The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife,” he added.
The CEO admitted in the meeting that he had flouted Nvidia’s code of conduct, which he himself had largely devised. Huang emphasized that the code of conduct was still in effect, but that mitigating circumstances would matter a lot. As Wired reported Huang’s statement, it “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door.”
Huang told staff that he’s in therapy and also said that he was grateful for a second chance at the company.
The CEO is now walking a difficult tight rope between reasserting his authority over one of the world’s most powerful and influential companies, and conceding that he may have made some mistakes. He also tackled the difficult question of President Trump’s role in his restoration. The President reportedly called Nvidia’s board directly to lobby for Huang’s return, but in his talk, Huang downplayed Trump’s role
Huang thanked the administration on Tuesday for “providing Nvidia with quick access to intelligence that he said helped the board determine that the national security risks the company faced in reinstating him were low,” the Wall Street Journal writes.
Huang will likely need the administration’s support as he weathers an upcoming wave of Congressional scrutiny from a newly Democrat-led government. The CEO is scheduled to appear for a public Senate Banking Committee hearing next week and, in the coming weeks, he will be called to appear for a number of different closed House hearings, including for the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.

Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Middlesbrough and Swansea City at the Riverside Stadium on Tuesday night; Will Lankshear returned to the starting line-up with the winning goal to send Boro back to the top of the table.
Tuesday 24 November 2026 21:48, UK
Will Lankshear was back among the goals as Middlesbrough cemented their position at the top of the Championship with a 2-1 win over Swansea City.
Lankshear had missed the final two games prior to the international break because of a hamstring injury, and was only afforded a late substitute appearance in Saturday's win over Bristol City.
Having been restored to the starting line-up at the Riverside, the Championship's leading scorer claimed his 14th league goal of the season to reestablish his side's lead in the second half after Joseph Opoku's driven finish had cancelled out Myles Peart-Harris' opener.
Lankshear's winner came nine minutes into the second half, but the England Under-21 international was also heavily involved in the slick passing move that led to Boro opening the scoring in the ninth minute.
Lankshear's first-time pass released Neto Borges into the left of the area and when he squared across the face of the box, Peart-Harris slotted home a first-time strike of his own to claim his first goal since joining Middlesbrough in the summer.
Boro's lead lasted 13 minutes, with Swansea levelling when Lankshear was at fault at the opposite end of the field.
The striker bundled over Elijah Just on the edge of the area to concede a free-kick. Ben Cabango's goalbound header was nodded off the line by Ashley Phillips, but the ball broke to Opoku, who drilled home an excellent low finish from the edge of the area.
Boro went close to regaining their lead when Riley McGree fired a first-time strike just wide from a corner, and threatened again just before the interval when Peart-Harris volleyed over at the back post after David Strelec flicked Borges' cross into his path.
Swansea remained a threat though, and six minutes into the second half Adilson Malanda played Eom Ji-sung onside as Opoku's through ball unpicked the Boro defence, only for goalkeeper Radek Vitek to burst from his line to keep out the midfielder's shot with his foot.
It was a crucial save as just three minutes later Boro were scoring their second goal at the other end. Callum Brittain's pass sent Peart-Harris breaking away down the right, and when he squared the ball across the face of goal Lankshear was left with the easy task of tapping home.
Sebastian Berhalter should have added a third goal with 18 minutes remaining, but after coming off the bench the American midfielder dragged a shot wide from the right of the area.
His fellow replacement, Max Arfsten, also wasted a good late opportunity, drilling a low strike straight at goalkeeper Lawrence Vigouroux.

But Dundee showed plenty of fight after the break and pulled one back through Joe Wright.

The visitors tried in vain to grab an equaliser and it was Hibs who were left satisfied by their first three points at home since beating Kilmarnock on April 4.
Despite being thrashed by Dundee United 4-0 at the weekend, Hibernian head coach Marink Reedijk decided to make only two alterations to his team, with Cadden and Thibault Klidje coming in.
Dundee manager Steven Pressley changed half of his outfield XI following the 8-0 humiliation to Hearts.
Owen Bevan was suspended and in came on-loan Bournemouth defender Matai Akinmboni for a full debut while Joe Wright, Brad Halliday, Joe Bevan and Ashley Hay started.
Hibs played on the front foot as they looked to start repairing the damage from the weekend's demoralising loss.
On a rare start, Togo international Klidje was lively and saw a header crash into the side-netting before hitting a harmless snap-shot straight at Dundee goalkeeper Owen Goodman.
From a short corner routine Hibs worked space for Cadden on the edge of the box from Josh Mulligan's lay-off and his driving effort whistled just past a post.
Dundee were desperate to keep it tight at the back but offered little going forward. Just when it looked like they were beginning to settle Hibs hit them two goals in three minutes before the break.
The first came in the 40th minute when Boyle fired a penalty past Goodman after being tripped by Ryan Finnigan.
Cadden then found the top corner with a sublime curling effort from his left foot just outside the box. It was another short corner routine that saw Miguel Chaiwa set up the wing-back.
Despite the hammer blow of losing two goals in quick succession before the break, Dundee demonstrated at the start of the second half that they were not going to roll over.
Pressley's side upped their intensity as they searched for a goal to get themselves back in the game and that arrived in the 67th minute courtesy of Wright.
Substitute Callum Jones' free-kick should have been put away by Ryan Astley but the ball broke back to Wright and he slammed the ball high into the net from six yards.
That set up a tense finish but Hibs desperately held on for a rare home victory.

Norwich's impressive run of victories came to an end as QPR held them to a 1-1 draw at Carrow Road.
The Canaries had won their previous five Championship fixtures but had to come from behind to pick up a point this time around after Harvey Vale had fired the visitors in front just before the break.
Philippe Clement's side were quickly back on level terms in the second half through a well-taken Anthony Musaba effort, but were well contained after that as Rangers registered a well-deserved point.
After a slow start, the match burst into life with a flurry of activity around the mid-point of the first half.
Norwich thought they had taken the lead on 19 minutes when Harry Darling got a touch on an in-swinging Jacob Wright free-kick but the effort was ruled out for offside.
Andre Brooks then saw a low shot from the edge of the area come back off the upright, while at the other end Dan Grimshaw did well to palm away a goal-bound effort from Vale.
Rangers were giving the hosts plenty to think about and took the lead four minutes before the break when Vale made another opportunity count.
The Republic of Ireland international had plenty to do after latching on to Kealey Adamson's pass but despite having Ruairi McConville and Darling in close attendance, he worked himself some space in the area before firing a powerful shot past Grimshaw.
Norwich were back on level terms within three minutes of the restart after a poor clearance by goalkeeper Pierce Charles was punished. It went straight to Musaba, who played a quick one-two with Mathias Kvistgaarden before confidently finding the roof of the net.
Vale fired inches wide as Rangers sought a quick response while substitute Oscar Schwartau was foiled by a good save from Charles as the game entered its final 10 minutes.
Norwich continued to press for a winner but could find no way through as they drew a game for the first time this season.

The managers
Norwich's Philippe Clement:
"This team will never settle for a draw - they will always keep going for the win but in football it doesn't always happen.
"After going behind we showed the right mentality, got our goal and kept pushing them back, with the fans playing their part, but unfortunately we couldn't get the second goal we deserved.
"We were up against a well-organised side and knew it was going to be tough but I thought the momentum was with us in the first half too and we just needed a bit of luck.
"We had a goal ruled out through a very tight offside decision and then Andre (Brooks) hit the post.
"When we went behind it became an even tougher task because we know how difficult they are to break down but our response was really good with everyone playing their part, including the lads who came off the bench."
QPR's Julien Stephan:
"That's four points from two very tough away games, Millwall and Norwich, which is a very positive outcome and all credit to the players for that.
"We were up against a side who had won their previous five games, scoring 17 goals, and it was a very good performance, with a draw a fair result I feel.
"We started very well, both with and without the ball, playing with a good tempo, and scored a very good goal.
"Obviously we were disappointed to concede so early in the second half but the lads showed great character to stick to the game plan. They defended properly as a team and we also had some chances.
"I am lucky to have a special group of players here and although they are a young group I thought they showed great maturity out there to come away with a deserved point."

A cross missed by Krejci gave Derby's Filip Bilbija a sniff of goal but Krejci desperately hacked clear before the winger could shoot, Mohammed Fuseini lobbing over the loose ball.
Wolves returned to the attack where Andre lifted a rising effort comfortably over the bar.
Derby breached Wolves' back line again only to hit the woodwork.
Widell Zetterstrom's free-kick was won by Matt Clarke and Morris' shot hit Krejci before Fuseini crashed a shot against Jose Sa's head then against the outside of the bar.
Wolves responded by taking a 29th-minute lead through Armstrong.
Mane did brilliantly to shake off Clarke on the touchline before pulling it back for Tommy Doyle, whose shot was blocked, Armstrong tucking away the loose ball.
Armstrong was inches away when he stabbed wide from Bueno's diagonal pass.
Rafiki Said missed two chances to have doubled Wolves' lead just after half-time.
He headed over unmarked from Kieran Trippier's cross. Then he took the ball too close to Widell Zetterstrom in a one-on-one.
Wolves continued to threaten and Djiga headed powerfully over from Trippier's corner before Doyle's deflected chip sailed just wide.
An inviting cross from Mane was missed by Widell Zetterstrom but hit Said's thigh with the goal at his mercy, before Lopez and then Armstrong fired just wide.
Despite their dominance, Wolves had not forced a serious save from Widell Zetterstrom until he palmed Bueno's rising shot upwards.
Wolves finally got their long overdue second goal in the 74th minute.
Substitute Rodrigo Gomes drove in a fierce low cross and Mane gleefully steered home.
Armstrong made it 3-0 two minutes later, volleying into the far corner from just inside the box, though Widell Zetterstrom got a hand to it.

items.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
items.summary: AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants. But new resea
items.text:
AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants. But new research suggests that even the most advanced AI models struggle to reliably and safely navigate the messy details of people’s lives.
According to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Across all models tested, 15.7% of attempts failed at least one safety requirement, often leading to unintended consequences.
ShellBench was developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley, drawing on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to see how agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them.
The research comes as personal AI assistants are finding new popularity among developers, with Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic all fighting for a piece of the market with Muse, Dots, and Claude Duet, respectively.
In October, Meta said more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up its personal AI agent, Muse, within six weeks of launch, with about a quarter using it daily. That number is expected to grow as Meta implants Muse directly into Instagram DMs. Despite growing popularity among consumers, we still have little evidence about how reliable AI personal assistant products actually are.
ShellBench suggests that the unreliable nature of most everyday data sources still causes problems for many state-of-the-art systems. A successful agent should be able to navigate messy personal workspaces containing emails, calendar entries, spreadsheets, receipts, chat logs, outdated information, and phishing attempts, and figure out which information is relevant, what is private, and how to deliver the requested outcome without creating new problems.
It seems many of today’s AI agents are still not up to the task. Not only did even the highest performing agents frequently fail to meet the requirements of a task, but they also lacked consistency. When researchers ran each task three times under identical conditions, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, the highest-scoring model, nailed all three attempts less than half the time.
For autonomous assistants that are meant to run in the background without supervision, it’s a problem if users need to run an agent multiple times to get a result they trust.
Additionally, about 10% of otherwise correct attempts failed at least one safety criterion. Across the models and harnesses tested, agents failed to, for example, adequately account for a child’s school pickup 79.5% of the time. When handling laptop custody records, agents failed a requirement to identify and withhold a sensitive bank upload token in 18.6% of attempts. In another tasks, agents recommended duplicate or incorrect invoice payments 40.3% of the time.
The findings highlight a major issue for users adopting consumer personal AI assistants, namely that there’s always a risk that an agent can create more headaches in the course of trying to fulfill an otherwise ordinary request.
While AI benchmarks have largely focused on coding, professional work, or testing on specific tasks, ShellBench is attempting to evaluate how models perform on multi-step personal tasks within different agent harnesses — the software that controls how a model accesses information, uses tools, and takes actions.
While the researchers found model choice had a greater overall impact on performance than harness choice, among the more capable models, AI agent performance became more dependent on the harness.
For example, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra outperformed Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 when operating within the Pi harness, but it performed worse when both models were tested within Claude Code.
Meta’s Muse Wonder Full scored 56% in Pi, but only 38.1% in Claude Code. Meta’s Muse Wonder 1.0, meanwhile, averaged a success rate of 39.7% across the five harnesses tested.
Notably, while the researchers tested models from Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic, they didn’t evaluate them within the native harnesses of Muse, Dots, or Claude Duet, so the results may not be representative of the experience millions of consumers are having with the product today.
TechCrunch has reached out to Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic and the researchers in the study.

items.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
items.summary:
Shopping with AI is becoming less of a futuristic idea and more of something companies expect us to do. Walmart is the latest retailer making that shift, teaming up with Meta to let customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent.
The partnership, announced Tuesday, gives shopper
items.text:
Shopping with AI is becoming less of a futuristic idea and more of something companies expect us to do. Walmart is the latest retailer making that shift, teaming up with Meta to let customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent.
The partnership, announced Tuesday, gives shoppers another way to find products, compare prices, and make purchases without browsing Walmart’s website themselves. Instead, customers can simply tell Muse what they are looking for and let the AI do the work.
The announcement highlights how differently Walmart and Amazon are approaching AI shopping. While Amazon has taken steps to stop third-party AI agents from making purchases for customers, Walmart is leaning into the idea.
To get started, users open the Muse app, sign in to their Walmart account, and return to the assistant to begin shopping. They can ask it to find specific products, compare options, or track down deals. Once a customer makes a request in Muse, the assistant sends it to Walmart, which returns relevant products and helps build a shopping cart.
Walmart says it has built privacy protections into the experience. For instance, Muse doesn’t get access to a customer’s Walmart shopping history or other personal information. Shoppers can also set spending limits, require approval before purchases, and review orders placed by the agent.
Plus, the company notes users can always delete their agent’s profile if they want to.
The experience is powered by Walmart’s Agent Gateway, a new system that allows outside AI assistants to connect directly with the retailer’s online store. This launched in October, and the company is planning to open it up to more developers and AI platforms, meaning Muse could eventually be just one of several assistants capable of shopping Walmart’s online store.
Walmart is not the only company teaming up with Meta’s Muse. Instacart also recently joined forces with the AI assistant.
Beyond Muse, Walmart has recently rolled out more AI-powered features to its own shopping assistant, Sparky.
Some of the newer additions include turning handwritten shopping lists into shopping carts, using photos and voice commands to find products, and helping customers get around their local store. Shoppers can search for an item and use a pin on the store map to see exactly which aisle it’s in. There’s also a “Flash Price Tag” button that makes the item’s shelf label light up.

items.summary:
Pochettino leads Man Utd fury at Yoro red card ruling
- Published

Yoro was sent off eight minutes into
items.text:
Pochettino leads Man Utd fury at Yoro red card ruling
- Published
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has questioned the competence of video assistant referee officials after defender Leny Yoro had his red card overturned by the Football Association.
Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday after bringing down Aleksander Isak just outside the United penalty area.
United sources say they have conclusive proof it was impossible for Isak to reach the ball after he took a heavy touch, that it would have run on to goalkeeper Senne Lammens and Yoro should not have been punished for denying a goalscoring opportunity.
Pochettino said he had some sympathy with referee Sam Barrott but he is livid at how the situation played out.
"I am very disappointed," the Argentine said. "This type of thing can never happen.
"We can accept the referee can make a mistake. But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? Are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play 11 by 11? No.
"We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be at the level to drive [it]. We accept that the technology is there but what are they doing?"
United are furious at both the nature of the audio of the incident, and referees' chief Howard Webb defending referee Barrott's decision and the VAR John Brooks' reinforcing it on the Mic'd Up programme, which was shown on Sky Sports.
They intend to take the matter up with both the Premier League and ProRef.
It is the second time this season United been on the wrong end of a major VAR error.
Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland's winner in the Manchester derby at Old Trafford on 13 September was allowed to stand even though a clearly offside Enzo Fernandez was interfering with play.
There has been no apology from Webb on this occasion.
Instead, he has doubled down on the call, saying: "I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball."
United sources claim this interpretation is wrong.
The club are unhappy at the speed the on-field decision was confirmed. It is thought United used data around Isak's top speed and his chances of reaching the ball in their defence of Yoro to the FA. They claim this could have been done "within minutes" of the incident occurring.
This is not the only bone of contention at Old Trafford around the incident.
Pochettino also pointed out Liverpool forward Bradley Barcola was too close to the United wall from the resulting free-kick and Dominik Szoboszlai's opening goal should have been disallowed.
"No-one talked about [the fact] that the goal wasn't legal," said Pochettino. "Barcola was touching our wall. It must be disallowed.
"We need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce it and to say, the decision wasn't good. And now, the three points, where are the three points?"
Webb defends Yoro red card
What referee's chief Webb said about the incident on the Mic'd Up programme.
"There's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.
"That was the referee's call made on the field, and then the VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn't.
"That if there was any doubt, then it was doubt.
"It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. and
"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.
"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable. Certainly not clearly wrong."

items.title: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself
items.summary: As AI assistants evolve into more capable agents that can access our files, emails, calendar, browser, and more, the amount of trust we’re expected to place in AI companies is growing. One startup called Maple, co-founded by a former Apple engineer who worked on privacy-preserving technologies, is t
items.text:
As AI assistants evolve into more capable agents that can access our files, emails, calendar, browser, and more, the amount of trust we’re expected to place in AI companies is growing. One startup called Maple, co-founded by a former Apple engineer who worked on privacy-preserving technologies, is taking a different approach with its AI app, where users’ data remains private — even from the company itself.
“We wanted to build something that was not only encrypted but also could be proven, and that people could go look at the open-source code, and then they could look at what we call trusted execution environments,” explains Maple co-founder and CEO Mark Suman. “They can look at and verify the code that’s running on our servers, so they don’t really have to take our word for it.”
“They can audit everything themselves and know how their data is being handled,” he adds.
The idea of trust is Maple’s larger theme, as the startup proposes that there’s a way to build an AI app where consumers don’t have to trade privacy for convenience, as its competitors often require with their invasive privacy policies, data collection practices, and sometimes even training on users’ personal data.
Instead of asking users to trust that Maple won’t misuse their personal data, it’s attempting to build a business where it can’t access that data in the first place.
Like other AI apps on the market, Maple allows users to engage in a chat experience where they ask questions and get answers. Meanwhile, its newly launched desktop app, Maple Work, offers a more agentic experience where the AI can control your computer, work with your files and apps, and control your browser to get online tasks handled.
With the company’s recently closed $5.3 million round, it’s moving on to its next product — a cloud-based agent that will be able to continue its work even if your computer isn’t on. This addition would make Maple more competitive with other popular consumer AI services, like Meta’s Muse, Instinct, and other AI agents that work over chat.
The oversubscribed seed round was led by EPIC Ventures, with participation from Draper Associates, Planetary VC, and Epoch VC, and follows a pre-seed angel round of under a million. Maple plans to raise a Series A in the first half of 2027, given the investor interest.
Suman, who previously spent six years at Apple, already had a background where AI and privacy overlapped, he tells TechCrunch.
At Apple, he worked on AI and machine learning with a particular focus on computer vision. Given Apple’s stance on consumer privacy, the challenge he faced was building products that would protect people’s identity while benefiting from computer vision techniques. His co-founder, Anthony Ronning (CTO), has a background in defense tech, security, and networking.
Ronning started the company that later became Maple AI back in 2023, initially as a privacy-focused fintech. When Suman teamed up with Ronning in August 2024, the idea to create Maple AI was born. The following January, the product became available to the public as a mobile app.
The app offers a familiar interface for those used to AI chatbots, but under the hood it runs a variety of open models, including versions of DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Inkling from Thinking Machines, Google’s Gemma, and OpenAI’s GPT OSS. Users can pick and choose the models they want or, for a simpler experience, just toggle between a quick model and the more powerful one.
The models themselves run inside a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) — meaning a server with hardware encryption on it — within a U.S.-based data center. (Maple also offers support for European customers through a partner that runs its server in Europe).
“We actually don’t have access to [the data] while it’s inside the TEE,” explains Suman. “The data gets encrypted first on your device using a unique password that’s only known by you, the user — we don’t have access to it. It then goes into this TEE, and it gets decrypted inside there. The AI does its thing, and then it re-encrypts it with your password and sends it back to you,” he continues. “So we provide an end-to-end experience that’s very easy for the user, but we actually don’t have access to the raw data as it’s in flight or even when it’s at rest,” he adds.
This allows Maple to protect its users’ data, even from outsiders — like if hackers breached its system or the government came with a subpoena, for instance. All it could do would be to hand over an encrypted file.
“We just simply don’t want access to it,” Suman says of customers’ data. “That’s not part of our business model. And we also don’t want it to be part of our threat model.”
With the new desktop app, Maple is looking to small businesses who may want to benefit from AI without the data privacy risks. Inside the app, there’s an integration store where users can connect with other apps, like their Gmail or calendar. The desktop app can also spin up a subagent that works inside another AI app you may have on your desktop, like Claude, Codex, or others that support the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). This allows customers to use their preferred AI app for specific tasks, without having to give it all their information — just what’s needed for the given task.
Next year, Maple plans to enter the enterprise market with pilot work, where it will offer its own version of zero data retention. (Maple doesn’t retain most of the customers’ data, but when it has to, that data is encrypted.) It’s now in the process of completing SOC 2 compliance and security audits to get ready for this expansion.
The company declined to share its registered customer numbers, but noted it’s seen 60x growth over the past three months, as people have been looking for ways to increase their security with AI.

Introducing Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B: Powering Agentic Coding and Private Knowledge Work
Today, we’re introducing Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an upgrade to Ternary Bonsai 2 27B with substantially stronger agentic coding, multi-turn tool use, and multi-step task execution. Based on Qwen3.8 27B, it retains
items.text:
Introducing Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B: Powering Agentic Coding and Private Knowledge Work
Today, we’re introducing Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an upgrade to Ternary Bonsai 2 27B with substantially stronger agentic coding, multi-turn tool use, and multi-step task execution. Based on Qwen3.8 27B, it retains the previous release’s 5.9 GB model footprint while significantly improving the capabilities developers need to build agents that work with private files and tools on-device. The result is by far the strongest AI model of its memory footprint for agentic workloads.
With Ternary Bonsai 2 27B, we brought stronger reasoning, visual understanding, and tool use to local devices. Since then, we’ve focused on making the model more effective across long sequences of tool calls: interpreting results, adjusting when a step fails, and maintaining the task’s objective through the whole interaction. This release also continues our work to make Bonsai more practical by addressing excessive thinking and repetitive loops in the previous model. Compared with Ternary Bonsai 2, Ternary Bonsai 2.5 completes tasks in fewer turns, uses fewer tokens, and delivers results faster and more accurately.
Agentic workflows are particularly sensitive to model degradation: small errors can compound across successive tool calls and derail an entire task. Ternary Bonsai 2.5 significantly narrows the performance gap to the full-precision base model while retaining its compact footprint. Preserving this behavior through longer tasks is an important milestone in improving the intelligence density of models.
We evaluated Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B against both Ternary Bonsai 2 27B and the full-precision Qwen 3.8 27B base model, as reported in the full whitepaper. We see marked improvements in agentic execution, coding, and multi-turn tool use, as shown in the table below.
On a single NVIDIA H100, Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B achieves a generation speed of 291 tokens/s with MTP and processes a 2,000-token prompt at 3,200 tokens/s. Even on a consumer-grade RTX 4090, it delivers 204 tokens/s with MTP and a prompt processing speed of approximately 3,060 tokens/s. The demos below follow complete local workflows, from the initial request through intermediate decisions to the final result.
For products, this creates room to build assistance directly into the applications where work already happens: a coding assistant working through issues in a private repository, a document application that prepares reviewable summaries, or a desktop assistant that handles recurring analysis. Local deployment lets those products process sensitive material on the user’s device. Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B strengthens the model capabilities behind that experience while keeping the compact footprint that makes it practical.
Platform Coverage
Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B runs on NVIDIA and Intel GPUs via llama.cpp and on Apple devices (Mac, iPhone, iPad) via MLX.
Model weights are available today under the Apache 2.0 License.
Full technical details of our compression, evaluation, and benchmarking processes are available in our whitepaper.
Work with Us
We work with teams to tailor Bonsai models to their applications, from post-training on domain-specific data to optimizing inference for target hardware. If you’re building AI products with tight memory, latency, or power requirements, we’d love to explore how Bonsai can help. Reach out at sales@prismml.com.

items.title: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbaske
items.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbasket’s Marisa Kabas.
Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
It’s also not because of ‘tech bro’ culture.
It’s also not because of ‘tech bro’ culture.
During the meeting, Huang reportedly called claims that President Donald Trump was directly involved in his reinstatement — an idea publicly promoted by Trump himself — “completely untrue.” He added, “Don’t think for a second politics played a role in the company. We are the most apolitical company,” according to Kabas.
Along with attempting to dismiss Trump’s involvement, Huang reportedly said he also didn’t return because he was a “tech bro” who was “above the law” or “above the code of conduct.” He added that, “no story has been more tortured than this one in human history,” Kabas reports. Instead, Huang said the Nvidia board “evaluated the entire situation,” while receiving assurance from the government that he posed no national security threat, according to the NYT.
Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on November 12th, following reports of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two employees, including vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell. On Monday, Nvidia announced that it had reinstated Huang as CEO, president, and member of the board — a decision the White House said Trump was “totally involved in.” Trump also confirmed that he worked with Vice President JD Vance and other officials to bring Huang back. A swath of tech leaders, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and former White House AI czar David Sacks, were also in favor of Huang’s return.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the government “has no reason to believe” Huang’s return poses a risk to national security, adding that the US attorney general “does not possess evidence” that he engaged in “unlawful conduct.” Nvidia is still facing an investigation over its accounting practices, according to Reuters. The company is also carrying out its own internal investigation surrounding reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot. Huang is set to testify before Congress on December 1st to answer questions about national security concerns, and Democrats are already planning to press Huang about his return, as well as Trump’s involvement.
Even after all this, Huang reportedly said he “doesn’t believe in succession planning.” He also acknowledged that he violated Nvidia’s code of conduct, adding that he is attending therapy daily, Bloomberg reports. “I made some terrible mistakes,” Huang said, according to the NYT. “I was unfaithful to Lori, and I hurt my kids and of course, I hurt all of you.”

The visitor said Umar Farouk Umar, 92, had grabbed
items.text:
Nigerian monarch, 92, suspended after sexual assault claims
- Published
One of Nigeria's best-known monarchs, the Emir of Daura, has been suspended from all official engagements and travel following allegations of sexual assault by a Polish tourist.
The visitor said Umar Farouk Umar, 92, had grabbed her chest during a tourism encounter and that she felt disgusted by the experience.
The allegation sparked widespread discussion across social media platforms, with many calling for the suspension of the emir and an investigation - calls the Katsina state government has now heeded.
Umar has not commented on the allegations or his suspension.
He is one of several emirs - a traditional role dating back to pre-colonial times - who still wield great cultural and religious influence in northern Nigeria, although they have lost their political power.
Daura, where Umar serves as emir, holds an extremely important position for the Hausa people who dominate northern Nigeria. It is widely regarded as their spiritual homeland and the origin of the Hausa royal lineage, serving as the core of Hausa origin mythology and the legitimate foundation of traditional authority.
Politicians routinely visit his palace for royal prayers and to gain his support.
On her Instagram page, the tourist said she had spent 30 days travelling around Nigeria before visiting the Emir's palace on 14 November.
She posted a video, which has since been deleted, in which a man who appears to be the emir is holding her hands in his lap.
After some moments she was heard saying: "Stop, stop" as the hands reached for her chest.
According to a statement, Katsina Governor Dikko Umaru Radda directed the immediate constitution of a committee to investigate the allegations.
The statement said the state government was taking the allegations seriously and would rely on the committee's findings to determine the appropriate course of action.
It said the committee's findings and recommendations would be fully implemented, stressing that justice would be served.
However, it did not disclose the membership of the investigative committee, its terms of reference or the timeline for submitting its report.
The emir has been on the throne since 2007, succeeding his brother Bashar dan Umaru, who reigned for 41 years.

The AI
items.text:
Anthropic’s stock fell below its IPO price of $83, trading as low as $76 a share by midday Tuesday, down nearly 12% from Monday’s close.
Falling below the IPO price is often seen as a negative signal because underwriters typically price offerings at a discount to their expected trading value.
The AI industry has been eagerly watching how Anthropic’s shares trade, with VCs and other observers saying its performance could serve as a barometer for how public market investors value the sector.
The dramatic slump comes less than a week after Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq at $111.50 a share. If its shares continue to trade poorly in the coming weeks, the slide could put pressure on private startup valuations and weaken IPO prospects for other AI companies.
Anthropic isn’t the only AI stock selling off on Tuesday. Nvidia fell more than 7% by midday, giving back some of the more than 30%-plus gain it posted Monday after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO.

A Zimbabwean national has been convicted by a court in South Africa of planning to go to fight in Ukraine.

Twenty-four-year-old Wesley
items.text:
Zimbabwean convicted in South Africa of trying to fight in Ukraine
- Published
A Zimbabwean national has been convicted by a court in South Africa of planning to go to fight in Ukraine.
The country has strict laws which restrict unauthorised involvement in overseas wars.
Twenty-four-year-old Wesley Sothole, who pleaded guilty, was handed a five-year suspended prison sentence and was ordered to be deported from South Africa.
He is one of five Zimbabweans who were arrested at OR Tambo Airport in Johannesburg on 8 November. South African prosecutors have not confirmed which side the Zimbabweans allegedly intended to fight for.
Sothole's four co-accused have yet to enter pleas and are due to return to the Kempton Park Magistrates' Court on 1 December for further plea and sentencing proceedings.
Another four Zimbabweans were arrested at a hotel in Johannesburg at the same time in a joint operation and are facing a different court process.
The investigation has involved South African police, Interpol and other international law enforcement agencies.
South Africa's Foreign Military Assistance Act was passed in 1998 at a time when the government was concerned about members of the former apartheid security services going to fight elsewhere in Africa.
There has been growing concern across Africa over the recruitment of its citizens to fight in the war in Ukraine, with some reportedly being lured to Russia by promises of lucrative civilian employment.
A Ukrainian intelligence assessment estimated earlier this year that more than 1,700 people from 36 countries in Africa have been recruited to fight for Russia.
Some have been captured and are being held as prisoners of war.
In March, Kenya estimated that 252 of its citizens had been illegally conscripted in Russia.
Kenyan Foreign Minister Musalia Mudavadi visited Moscow to address the issue. He said an agreement had been reached for Russia to stop recruiting Kenyan nationals.
In the same month, Zimbabwe said that 15 of its nationals had been killed after being recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine, with more than 60 still trapped on the frontlines.
The previous month, South Africa secured the return of 17 of its nationals who were allegedly tricked into joining the war.
In December last year, South African authorities arrested five people, including a journalist, for allegedly recruiting people to join the war.
South Africa's government said it condemned "the exploitation of young vulnerable people by individuals working with foreign military entities".
Ukraine has also been recruiting foreign nationals, including from Africa.
Additional reporting by Khanyisile Ngcobo in Johannesburg.
